**Result.** Over a field of characteristic 0, every `120 × 120` matrix `M` indexed by the E8 lines with `rank M = 9`, `M_tt ≠ 0` and `M_ts = 0 ⇔ t ⊥ s` (t ≠ s) is **B-form** (`D₁GD₂ + cβᵀ`, rank-one biclique with `c_uβ_s = 0` on orthogonal pairs) **or in the A2 family** of #2784. Both families occur (exact members in `checks/a2e8.py`). This is the existence step ("Conjecture B\*") that #2784 left open.

- **PROVEN** from: Theorem G (CONJB / #2784 §3; span facts S1, S2 CHECKED), Theorem P (pinning) and Theorem A (an orthogonal pair in `Σ_a` or `Σ_b`; all 2025 E8 frames P-compatible, all 3780 orthogonal pairs in a frame, CHECKED), Theorem S, Theorem Σ, Theorem R.
- **Theorem S** (`Σ_a ∩ Σ_b ≠ ∅`): reduction PROVEN; finite step = a 56-line point/line incidence problem, CHECKED: kissat 4.0.4 UNSAT, standard drat-trim VERIFIED, regenerated by `verify.sh` for `f₁ = 0..15` (all 120 under `FULL=1`).
- **Theorem Σ** (`Σ_a ≠ ∅` or `Σ_b ≠ ∅`): PROVEN from S, A, G and CHECKED (S3′), (W2).
- **Theorem R** (`Σ_a = Σ_b = ∅` is empty): reduction PROVEN; finite step CHECKED: the pinning-model CNF (56 784 variables, 3 513 012 clauses) is regenerated byte-identically (sha256 pinned), kissat UNSAT with `--factor=false --preprocessfactor=false`, DRAT proof shipped xz-compressed (11.7 MB; 163 MB raw, sha256 pinned), standard drat-trim VERIFIED (shipped proof: 137 s). `FULL=1` also re-solves (≤ 20 min) and drat-trims a fresh proof. The auxiliary C checker `rupc.c` (RUP-only, deletions honoured, RAT rejected) agrees; drat-trim is the reference.
- Rule soundness of the model: one-line proofs in the card text; `soundtest.py` finds 0 violated clauses on true data (A2 members, 5 parameter draws on 5 triangles; B-form), and a mutation control (one flipped sign) is caught.
- Independent read-only audit: re-verified both certificates with drat-trim, regenerated the CNFs byte-identically, confirmed the soundness test catches a flipped rule (RECORDED; the two fixes it asked for are applied: characteristic 0 is stated, the A2 parameter is varied).

**Downstream (case (c) on E8).** With #2784 (A2-family floors, E8 ≥ 72), case (c) reduces to decoders on B-form realisations. Closed there: A2 family (#2784). For B-form, the working cards (not shipped) have: a term with `p ∝ c` and `q ∝ β` costs ≥ 64; `|supp c| = 1` (the #2321 / #2385 `K_λ` family) ≥ 64 modulo a CHECKED puncture census; the generic 8-clique type ≥ 65 for sampled values. **Not closed:** B-form with all `x_j, y_j ≠ 0` and `|supp c| ≥ 2`, non-generic `c, β`, singular `D`, `m ≥ 10`. So the E8 floor 72 for all rank-9 square decoders is **not** proven.

**Relation to philippeVV's open item (R1)** (Discussion #1587, follow-up 8, `decoder-law/lift-family-2` @ 93766d7d: "every rank-9 completion is a lift"). The lift normal form, credit machinery and census are theirs; nothing here uses them. Their completions (`decoder-law/README.md`) have `N_aa = 1`, `N_ab = 0` for `a ⊥ b` and non-orthogonal entries **free** (zeros allowed), a larger class than our iff pattern; our theorem covers only completions with all non-orthogonal entries nonzero. It would give R1 for that subclass only if every B-form and A2 realisation is a κ-lift, which we have not compared (their R3 covers dependent supports). So R1 does **not** follow. Remaining for R1: (i) show B-form ∪ A2 ⊆ lifts; (ii) drop the iff assumption: Theorem G survives (CONJB §5), but pinning (Theorem P), the NON rule and the S-step use nonzero entries, so both SAT models must be rebuilt and re-certified. Not attempted.

**Not claimed.** P112 / P104 (P112 Theorem R certification is in progress and nothing is claimed; P104 has few P-compatible frames); positive characteristic; formal-kernel check.

**Overlap.** A search of PR bodies for rank-9 / rank-nine realisation classifications found none besides #2784 (A2 family, same author) and #1212 (rank 8 only).

Verify: `bash verify.sh [outdir]` (numpy, sympy, kissat 4.0.4, drat-trim, cc, xz); default run re-solves and drat-trims the Theorem S step, regenerates and hash-checks both CNFs, checks the shipped proof's hash, and runs the soundness test; `FULL=1` adds the Theorem R re-solve and drat-trim.

**Status: research note with exact finite computations and written proofs (not a SAT/DRAT proof). No κ claim, no supplier word.** Only `research/one-sided-decoders-all-m/` is added; nothing existing is changed.

## What this proves (scope is the claim)

Model of #2338 / #2277 / #2724 / #1224: exact masked decoders `N = Σ_{j≤m} p_j q_jᵀ` of the **Gram realisation** of the P112 pattern, field of **characteristic 0**, dense pairing table `B`, cost `Σ_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j]`. **Case (b): one factor outside `col M`** (the other in `col M`), **every number of terms `m`**. Reduced to the `(y, U)` form; the decoder is a lift `S ⊇ 𝒞` of the root code, `cost ≥ cost_w(S)` (min-weight basis).

* **R1 (CHECKED + PROVEN).** ε-free one-sided P112 decoders cost **≥ 64 for every `d = dim(𝒞 ∩ S_{≤7})`**: exact DP for `d ≤ 6`, an LP with exact integer dual certificates for `d = 7, 8` (`lp3.py`), re-derived by an independent symmetrised LP with exact rational duals (`symlp.py`); the multiset enumeration is complete (`enum.py`: none for `d ≤ 6`, one at `d = 7`, seven at `d = 8`, all killed).
* **R2 (Theorem U′).** The cost-64 ε-free decoder is **unique**: the coordinate decoder (8 terms `(e_j, W_j)`). Cost-65 decoders have at most one non-full correction; the cost-66 case is reduced to six OPEN `d = 8` weight multisets.
* **R3 (corrections).** Lemma P: a *full* corrected term (`U = F2⁹`) is absorbed at no cost. **Corrected cost ≥ 64 whenever at most 2 corrected terms of the normalised decoder are non-full** (normalise = merge proportional corrected terms and absorb full ones, repeated until stable; terminates since (#terms, #full corrected) drops lexicographically; the version for raw decoders is the lift-level form R4 with `I` = all corrected terms); in general `≥ 64 − max(0, n_nf − 2) ≥ 58`. The **root-swap family attains 64 exactly** with `n_nf = 1, 2, 3, 4` (exact `P·Y = C`), so `Δ ≥ n_nf` is tight.
* **R4 (lift level).** Every `S ⊇ 𝒞_{X_I}` has `cost_w(S) ≥ 64 + min(|I|, 2)`; every lift of the E8 root code has `cost_w ≥ 66`.
* **R5.** Lemma N (≤ 2 directions per 7-flat after removing ≤ 4 lines; exact counts for `|L| = 1, 2`, an upper bound for `|L| ≤ 4`, and an independent C implementation) and the Pencil Lemma (`d ≤ 2`).
* Gain-law reading (philippeVV, Discussion #1587 follow-up 6): in this class the gain on P112 is at most 48 (`112 − 64`).

## Open residue (stated exactly, not claimed)

`Δ ≥ n_nf` for `n_nf ≥ 3`: at `n_nf = 3` exactly six `d = 8` multisets of the weight-≤7 basis remain (`[7^5,6^5,1]`, `[7^6,6^4]`, `[7^8,5,4,1]`, `[7^8,5,5]`, `[7^8,6,3,1]`, `[7^8,6,4]`). Not claimed here.

## Not covered (stated up front)

* Case (c) (rank-9 realisations, see #2784), two-sided decoders, P104 and other units, `B` of rank ≥ 10, positive characteristic.
* **Imported (merged results, not re-derived):** Gram realisation (#1212 Theorem 1, plus a diagonal normalisation); dense table (#2338 Theorem R, DRAT-checked there). The parabolic-flat fact is proved in the README (C3).
* Not DRAT / Lean: written proofs plus exact Python/C computations, re-runnable.

## Labels and verification

PROVEN / CHECKED / RECORDED / IMPORTED / OPEN per claim in the README. `bash verify.sh` (about 12–15 minutes, two processes, no SAT) re-runs every exact check (DP, enumeration, LP certificates, Lemma N in two implementations, the root-swap family) and asserts them in `checks/check_logs.py`; fresh `git archive` export: 34 PASS / 0 FAIL in 714 s (logs in `evidence/logs`).

## Overlap

Scanned the 1,000 most recent PRs (titles), 119 decoder-related bodies and 100 recent Discussions: no ε-free one-sided floor for all `m`, LP/charging certificates, uniqueness statement, root-swap family or Lemma N. Nearest: #1224 (model), #1180 (both factors in the root code), #1633, #1815, #1609, and our #2338 / #2277 / #2724 (this is the every-`m` extension of #2724's case (b) at `m = 9`, by a different method).

I compile the selected schedule from David Arias's PR2753 into finite macrocode and execute it with one active frame, permanent stream roles and shared numerical banks. Before each child I serialize the successor PC and parent state; after return I restore those roles and continue at that PC. I also erase the root's owned markers and templates. The source-level proof retains O_q(V_root)+F_q space and O_q(V(n+w)) local work on the pinned input/root-coupling domain.

The implementation covers node setup, remainder peel, source-bound residuals, private COPY/XOR, IDLE, bridge/exchange and recursive CALL/RETURN. I forbid new physical Tape/Arena construction during completed blocks and use explicit scratch leases. Production calls the retained selected coefficient and descriptor routines.

Evidence includes:

- A complete 9,216-bit recursive GL2(F2) program: 5,859 macros, 12 child calls/returns and 156 residuals, with the source recursive Invocation constructor disabled.
- A complete 31,104-bit four-family GL2(F3) program: 192 MOVE, 96 COPY and 384 IDLE residuals. Independent oracles check each private COPY before cancelling XORs, both intermediate sweeps and the final endpoint.
- Actual selected rank-42 coefficients and typed child descriptors, exact parent restoration, scratch ownership controls, a nonzero remainder peel and a two-digit atom swap.

I corrected the earlier parent-identity verifier gap reported by [starship-s](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-18960884). I reproduced the 214 accepted wrong-parent boundaries, then added identity checks before deterministic projection on both paths, twelve wrong-parent controls and three generated-call binding controls. I retain the auditor's reported Linux timeout on the old logical replay as a limitation; current validation details and receipts appear in VALIDATION.md and RESULT.json.

All seven registered commands passed under Python 3.12.15/macOS arm64 after that correction, before the final upstream refresh. The recursive and four-family controller replays took 104.67 and 321.60 seconds. At submission I merged canonical main `c719a5e0b3a6760a6fdf5d5af82d6ff2399329e5` and retained exact compatibility pins for its sole selected-record change, a UTF-8 verifier hash. Normal/-O Frame and continuation checks passed with the new authentication controls. Fresh complete-run attempts timed out: first in continuation at 30 seconds (then passed alone in 48.08 seconds), then in macro_nested under an experimental 240-second allowance. I restored the original registered budget. The controller and payload oracles have no changes from the full pass; I claim no complete pass after the refresh, fresh Linux pass or hosted-CI pass. VALIDATION.md records both outcomes.

I have not materialized the astronomical selected GL64 instruction word or expanded the retained primitives into one microtransition table. The reduced fixtures use their stated small grammars; the selected junction check uses a controlled body. Stronger H2 primitives, outer-wrapper composition and supplier admission remain separate. I make no exponent or frontier change.

I retain 97 byte-exact source exports and credit David Arias (PR2753), ywz65 (PR2635), my PR2769 codec and their predecessor notices. I used substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; I claim no independent human or proof-assistant verification.

[Canonical scope and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-18958887).

Closures-only follow-up of #2639 (open; this PR is based on it and uses its tools and Theorem M8 as stated there). **No κ claim.**

#2639 §4 lists `m ≤ 7` at `48 ≤ p ≤ 56` as open. This note closes it, in the same setting (punctured E8 units, Model C: dense `B`, column-space factors), so **every `p` with `48 ≤ p ≤ 56` is closed for every `m`** (`m ≥ 8`: #2639 Theorem M8 with its Case-B census; `m ≤ 7`: this PR).

* **Reduction (PROVEN from #2639's E7q, Lemma G/H/R, monotonicity in `P`).** `48 ≤ p ≤ 53`: a root with `q ≤ Q(p)` is closed by E7q, otherwise all `q_γ ≥ 6`; `54 ≤ p ≤ 56`: `q ≤ 16` is closed by Lemma R (`m = 7`: cost ≥ 35 ≥ need(p)), otherwise all `q_γ ≥ 17`. `m ≤ 7` then needs a Lemma-G failure, i.e. SAT of one CNF per rank-7 flat type: (I-a) `P = 53`, all `q_γ ≥ 6` (covers 48–53); (I-b) `P = 56`, all `q_γ ≥ 17` (covers 54–56).
* **Result (RECORDED from the author's working card; sample re-checked).** All 8 flat types are UNSAT-VERIFIED for both families: every leaf of the orbit trees is kissat + drat-trim VERIFIED against its own CNF, or a counting leaf (`|T| > P`); no SAT, no TIMEOUT. Per-leaf tables with the md5 of every leaf CNF, state files and run summaries are shipped.
* **`verify.sh`** (≈ 15 min, one core, `nice 10`): manifest/pins; tallies and arithmetic; rebuilds the option sets for 4 of the 8 types from scratch (E8 lines, 440,880 rank-7 flats); encoding checks (leaf CNF vs. direct numpy test, 880 sets, kissat); tree coverage (`c3`: each orbit tree re-walked with an oracle leaf, every recorded leaf visited, none missing; CHECKED); then regenerates 60 leaf CNFs per (type, family), compares md5 with the recorded runs and sha256 with pins, and re-solves 15 per (type, family) with kissat + drat-trim. `FULL=1` does every leaf and the coverage of all 8 types (hours).
* **Proofs shipped:** 12 small leaf DRAT proofs (xz) with sha256 of proof and CNF, drat-trimmed by `verify.sh` against regenerated CNFs; the other leaf proofs are RECORDED (md5-pinned CNFs, regenerable).
* **Imported from #2639 (open), labels as there:** E7q PROVEN from CHECKED data; Lemma H PROVEN; Lemma R PROVEN from card-verified data; Theorem M8 PROVEN from RECORDED data; Case-B census RECORDED. They are not re-derived here; `Q(p)` and `need(p)` are recomputed by `c1`.
* **Not claimed / not re-run:** `p = 47` with `m ≤ 7` stays open. The other ≈10⁴ leaf proofs are not shipped (tens of GB); their verdicts are RECORDED, regenerable on demand.
* **Overlap:** a search of PR bodies found no other closure of these punctures; #939 / #1171 treat star label decoders, a different class.

Package: `research/punctured-e8-48-56/` (README with PROVEN / CHECKED / RECORDED labels, `verify.sh`, `checks/`, `sat/`, `data/`, `evidence/`, `MANIFEST.sha256`, `SOURCES.json`).

independent check of open PR #2530 by zxv (head `b4012098`; T74 source-partner lifetimes; conditional
κ ≈ 0.0017137379).

The checks use only the standard library. They read 38 pinned git objects from PR2530, PR2462, PR2435, PR2269 and
PR2474 as data, and never import or run PR code. **No defect was found**; every PR2530 number re-derived here
reproduces.

**What this adds.** Four concurrent audits cover parts of #2530: #2664, #2661, #2656 and #2669. As of 2026-10-15
22:26 UTC (heads re-confirmed), none of them checks the following for #2530:
1. **Both words end to end.** They are exact on all 646 dirty inputs, forward and dual, through the 4,529-item
   cleanup and the target endpoint. A dual-only mutant shows that the dual replay adds coverage: the forward replay
   accepts it and the dual rejects it.
2. **Physical stock** 66,814. This is a consistency check: this author contributed to the stock rule.
3. **The endpoint and κ.** A directed-rounding enclosure accepts `C = 0.001713737921547504346752` and rejects
   C + 1e-24. The grid conditions for `κ = C − 1e-70 − 1e-46` hold, given the author-checked outer inequalities.
4. **The verifier overrides**, diffed against PR2462's verifier.
5. **R-g owner charts:** 7,023 charts.

It also corroborates those audits with another implementation: the handoffs and gates (#2664), the profile recount
(#2656), the windows (#2661, #2669), and the fill R-a..R-e and idle histogram (#2661).

**Fill order dependence.** It records how #2530's fill depends on its call order:
- Under PR2462's order, 60,541 roles leave their windows.
- Of the 665 adjacent swaps of calls from different replicas, 238 keep the fill legal.

**Findings for the PR2530 author (non-blocking):**
- The 24-digit outer endpoint is stated only in the sibling `t74-owner-consolidation` README. It forgoes about
  7.0e-25 of κ.
- The `prefix_l1` denominators are uncharged by `prefix_bits`. This is inherited and well within headroom.

**What later claims can use (compared at heads; heads re-confirmed 2026-10-15 22:26 UTC):**
- **Word checks:** #2571 and #2575.
- **Order and window checks:** #2575, #2588 and #2679.
- **#2571's head** uses an order shifted by s = 4; its PR body is stale.
- **No later claim reuses #2530's fill.** #2802 (opened 22:23 UTC) was not compared.

**Not re-derived (author-checked):**
- the native `K_op` identity for the 12 lenders applied in both the prelude and the handoff;
- the 63 outer inequalities;
- strict global admission;
- the binding of the words to the receipts' `canonical_word_sha256` (a hash of a file the native replay produces);
- the receipts' `prefix_l1` values.

**Controls:**
- 148 negative controls, 99 distinct. Each must be rejected by its named rule, and the run asserts that this rule
  fires.
- 3 positive controls, on PR2462's words and endpoint.
- 62 mutations of the checker itself (local-only): every one makes the run fail.

This extends the words of #2751 (@tekuuu, head `4cfbb0cc`) with seven retired-lender aliases. Five need only exact refits. The other
two are opened by moving two existing borrows onto free retired lenders.

The new conditional κ is **0.001717794984118634663826999…**. The exact rational is `0.001717794984118634663827 - 10^-46 - 10^-70`;
the selected frontier is unchanged.

| over | margin |
|---|---|
| #2751 (tekuuu) | +6.53397770208325718e-7 (exact 326698885104162859/(5·10^23)) |
| #2766 (DavidAriasC) | +5.38010651632355557e-7 (exact 538010651632355557/10^24) |
| #2767 (jeremykothe2) | +5.38010651632355556055e-7 |

**What is new, and what is credited.**
- The certified frames contain, unchanged, #2766's frame refit of #2751's words: B1151 rank 6 -> 5. #2767 reaches the same κ by
  another route.
  - *Corrected after #2847:* the other 19 frame changes (A0-A11, B771/773/776/778/783/788, restore60) were credited to #2766 here by
    mistake. #2766's own words change only B1151. The 19 are this package's `refit5c` choices, and #2847 shows they are
    cost-neutral. The package README and `CLAIM.json` at `17b2ee6e` still carry the old wording.
- New here, worth +5.38e-7 over #2766/#2767:
  - **Five retired-lender aliases** (606<-550, 635<-551, 637<-552, 638<-553, 639<-562), made feasible by exact one-rank refits:
    +1.52e-7.
  - **Two hostee moves** that free two more lenders, plus the two aliases they enable (667<-401, 669<-403): +3.86e-7.

**Construction.**
- Every alias is of the kind of #2679's 653<-563 (philippeVV). A helper enters a retired lender's register through one B warp
  with an explicit invertible `G`, `G(U)=E`; the helper and its private register are gone.
- **Five aliases.**
  - Each lender's last gate drops from rank 6 to 5, its exact floor; each follower's first gate rises from rank 4 to 5, its exact
    ceiling. Both use #2679's frame-lattice tools.
  - The census on #2751's words found no fixed-frame pairs and 35 refit-feasible ones.
- **Hostee moves.** With every existing B-warp hosting treated as movable, the remaining rank-4 followers 667/669/670/671 can enter
  24 hosted lenders whose own lives end in A, but only if each hostee moves to a free retired lender. Only 564 and 565 qualify
  (floor 5, retired at B911/B912 before the hostees enter). That gives 192 augmenting paths, at most two extra aliases.
  - Chosen: warps 30/31 (#2226 borrows; their hostees enter at rank 5 already), moved 401 -> 564 and 403 -> 565.
  - 564/565's last gates are refit from rank 6 to 5. Both warp records are replaced in place, so op ids are kept.
  - 401/403 then take 667 and 669 at fixed frames (dim 4).
- The final program takes its certified optimal frames (#1186 toolkit). The 48 followers with a rank-1 entrance stay infeasible:
  every lender floor is at least 4.

**Result.**
- 408 helpers {4:26, 5:2, 7:62, 8:78, 9:240}, 72 buffers, 666 calls, 271728 roles; physical 66794.
- Local profile `{1:2382,2:648,3:268,4:128,5:26,8:8}`.
- The owner fill is #2751's fill with the seven helpers' 4662 roles removed (renumbered, every bin re-tiled as a prefix). Its
  pattern relaxation has the same optimum.
- Complete profile `{1:1603728,2:431568,3:185082,4:85248,5:27194,8:5328,32:1,48:26558}`; rank mass 4816512.

**Independent checks.**
- #2847 (@thakrarsagar): fresh standard-library code checks the seven stages over #2751 on both words. 28/28 rules pass and all 20
  negative controls are rejected, with no defect found. It reproduces the retired5/retired7 split and corrected the #2766 frame
  credit above.
- Followers 670/671 (@philippeVV, [comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2802#issuecomment-6203637793),
  checker `philippeVV/integer-mult-bounds@0610f3de`): no refit of the fixed gate list gives them a lender. With all 72 hostees
  movable, their 74 pairwise-overlapping lives would need the 72 registers whose floor is at most 5, and all of those already host.
  That leaves 0 augmenting paths, so a further alias needs a gate-level edit.

**Packaging.**
- Only `research/t74-joint-twelve-retired7/` is added. #2751's directory is byte-identical.
- The branch is based on #2751's head, so this PR contains #2751's commit until #2751 merges.
- The seven stages `refit5 -> alias5 -> refit5c -> refit7 -> hostmove2 -> alias7 -> refit7c` are new `rebuild_borrow` stages in the
  overlay, with exact structure checks. Each new state passes the auditor.
- Tamper controls: 71 per word. Every mutant re-derives its cleanup, and a stale-cleanup rejection counts as a failure:
  - lender refits undone (`warp frame mismatch`);
  - follower raises undone;
  - per move: lender reverted, move undone, warp before retirement, `G` wrong;
  - #2679's alias suite per alias;
  - corrupted certified frames.

**Status: research note with exact finite computations and written proofs (not a SAT/DRAT proof). No κ claim, no supplier word.** Only `research/a2-family-decoder-floors/` is added; nothing existing is changed.

## What this proves (scope is the claim)

Model of #2338 / #2277 / #2724: exact masked decoders `N = Σ_{j≤m} p_j q_jᵀ` of a pattern realisation (zero on orthogonal pairs, nonzero elsewhere on the diagonal and off it: the "iff pattern"), arbitrary factors over a field of characteristic 0, dense pairing table `B`, cost `Σ_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j]`.

* **A1/A2: the A2 family.** For P112, P104 and E8 there are rank-9 iff-pattern realisations that equal the Gram matrix except on the three rows of one A2 triangle, where each row is the Gram row rescaled by one factor on `N̄(u_i) ∩ O_{u_j}` and another on `N̄(u_i) ∩ O_{u_k}` (7 parameters plus diagonal scalings). They are **not of B-form** `D₁GD₂ + cβᵀ` (with `c_uβ_s = 0` on orthogonal pairs): a counterexample to our working "Conjecture B" for rank-9 realisations. Exact certificate (three random exact members per unit, plus the two tie members below).
* **Theorem G (PROVEN).** If the rows outside a set `X` of a rank-9 pattern realisation are Gram rows, it is B-form with `supp c ⊆ X`, or in the A2 family on an A2 triangle inside `X` (columns: transposed). **Lemma E (PROVEN)**: rank ≤ 8 on `V∖X` plus a rigid sub-unit (#1212 and extensions) gives Gram rows. The existence step ("every rank-9 realisation has such an `X`") is **OPEN** and not claimed.
* **Floors (F).** Every 9-term (square) decoder of **every** A2-family member, at all parameters and on all A2 triangles, costs **P112 ≥ 64, P104 (#968's unit) ≥ 56, E8 ≥ 72**. Triangle coverage: P112 one orbit of 896, E8 one orbit of 1120, P104 ≤ 28 orbits (all 28 representatives run). Case I (some row normal ∥ `e_9`) and Case II (none; II(b) by an exact class-level min-cost relaxation, 65 / 62 / 74 off the B-locus, 66 / 63 / 75 on it, using the checked fact that two merged column classes are co-killable only on `γ₂ = γ₃`); includes the E8 near-miss (the three punctured normals `r_1, r_2, r_3` are dependent).
* **Sharpness (S).** Exact tie decoders of cost **64 (P112)** and **72 (E8)** at the stated special parameter points (exact over Q, independently re-evaluated; the tie members are certified non-B-form); the generic members checked reach only 65 / 73. P104 sharpness is not claimed.
* **`m ≥ 10`, both factors in the realisation's two 9-dimensional spaces (M), off the B-locus `γ₂ ≠ γ₃`.** Cost ≥ **68 (P112), 64 (P104), 77 (E8)** (merge lemma + exact class-level min-cost relaxation). On the B-locus the relaxation is lower (62 / 58 / 70) and that case is **open**.

## Not covered (stated up front)

* **Decoders with factors outside `col M` / `row M` on the A2 family with `m ≥ 10` are NOT covered** (for `m = 10` they are exactly the one-sided frame-expansion decoders; only a heuristic search was done, which found ties and nothing proven).
* **Other rank-9 realisations**: this is one explicit family, not all of case (c). In particular nothing here bears on the co-star decoders (Discussion 1267, #1320) unless their realisation lies in the family.
* **`m ≥ 10` on the B-locus `γ₂ = γ₃`**: open (not claimed).
* Non-iff patterns, `B` of rank ≥ 10, other P104 units. Not claimed: that the A2 family is an irreducible component; the variant of the non-B-form statement without the orthogonal-pair condition.

## Labels (every step is in the README)

PROVEN: square-decoder normal form, merge lemma, A2 facts, the construction, Theorem G, Lemma E, the non-B-form argument, Case I and II(a). PROVEN from CHECKED: Case II(b) (row census parameter-free, column census treats `γ` symbolically; merged-kill fact; class-level relaxation) and `m ≥ 10` off the B-locus. CHECKED (exact computation): members with the iff pattern and rank 9; rank certificates (mod p, safe direction); span facts S1/S2; the unit census on all three units and all 28 P104 representatives; survivor-pair ranks; the row-puncture floors `P_k` (exact branch-and-bound on P112/P104, structural on E8); the tie decoders; exact optima at fixed members (65 / 64 / 73 / 72); the merged-kill fact (P112, E8, all 28 P104 representatives); the class-level relaxations; pair tables at the members checked (corroboration). **RECORDED (logs shipped, hash-pinned, headline lines asserted, not re-run):** the robust CP-SAT / CEGAR runs over all parameters (no square decoder ≤ 63 on P112, ≤ 71 on E8) and the all-parameter special-locus census behind the pair tables.

## Verification

`bash research/a2-family-decoder-floors/verify.sh /fresh/dir` (Python ≥ 3.11, `numpy`, `networkx`; one process at a time; no SAT solver). On a fresh `git archive` export: **102 PASS, 0 FAIL**, 941 s wall (15.4 min user CPU, one process at a time, `nice 10`; venv Python 3.14, numpy 2.5, networkx 3.7).

**What `verify.sh` re-runs:** units; survivor classes and survivor-pair ranks; S1/S2; exact A2 members and the non-B certificate on all three units; the unit census (replayed and compared line for line with the recorded logs) on the first triangle of each unit and all 28 P104 representatives; triangle-orbit counts; `P_k` and the case arithmetic; the merged-kill fact and the Case II(b) / `m ≥ 10` class-level relaxations (P112, E8, all 28 P104 representatives); the tie decoders and the tie members' certificates; exact optima at fixed members; pair tables at members (corroboration). **RECORDED, not re-run:** the CP-SAT / CEGAR logs and special-locus census (`evidence/logs/hunt-a2/`, pinned in `MANIFEST.sha256`).

## Overlap

Searched (2026-10-15): "A2 family / triangle / subsystem", "rank 9 / rank-9 / rank nine realisation", "non-B-form", "B-form", "Conjecture B", "square decoder", "decoder floor", "masked P112 decoder", "co-star", "rank-8 rigidity", "non-Gram rank" and the unit sizes. No PR body found that states an A2-family (non-B-form) rank-9 realisation, Theorem G / Lemma E, or these floors. Nearest: #2338 / #2724 (ours; case (c) open item and sibling), #1212 and extensions (rank 8 only), #2321 / #2385 / #2398 / #2515 (one fixed rank-9 P112 completion under a COPY-power cost). Bodies read, proofs not; discussions not searched.

Parents: #2338 (open item "factors outside `col M`, `m ≥ 9`", case (c)), #2724, #2639, #2277 (ours). Cited from their statements: #1212, #1389, #1399, #1419, #1425, #1616 (rank-8 rigidity, used only to state Lemma E), #968 (the P104 unit), #1224, #1180, #1320, D1267 (context, not covered).

# F-star residue class (ii): non-3-dichromatic zero digraphs - the matched-pivot floor, the fixtures' dichromatic structure, and a smallest-first falsifier search (no kappa)

## Scope

Kappa-blocker **KB5c** (explicit open request; scope changed from the drawn card and recorded in `TASK.json`): residue class **(ii) non-3-dichromatic zero digraphs** of open problem **F-star** of the merged `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` package ([PR 1590](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1590) by DreamingOfClouds, with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code assistance; section 7): `cert(M) >= floor(2v/3)` for every exact 3-total rational decoder `M = sum_j p_j q_j^T`. This is the residue [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717) by Aaron Wang (navinor) demoted as "zero digraphs that are not 3-dichromatic (Lemma MP then gives only `sum_i MAS(Z[C_i])`)" and left untouched by [PR 2747](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2747) by Aaron Wang (navinor), which closed residue class (i). Package `research/fstar-zero-digraph-residue-seede9937f18/`, registered replay `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed` on CPython 3.12.

The package does three things: (1) exact zero-digraph machinery (MAS over all subsets by DP, the exact Lemma MP value `max_c sum_i MAS(Z[C_i])` over all pivot maps `c : [v] -> D(t)`, dichromatic numbers of `Z` with and without the pivot constraint sets `D(t)`); (2) calibration on DreamingOfClouds' stored fixtures `tied_min` (12 lines) and `cex_min_1` (19 lines) reproducing every recorded anchor, then the exact dichromatic structure of both zero digraphs (the open question 2 of PR 2717); (3) a smallest-first adversarial search for the first instance where the matched-pivot value falls below `floor(2v/3)` (the open question 1 of PR 2747, which is exactly this class's floor question). **F-star itself is not proved and not refuted here.** Every claim is labelled PROVEN, CHECKED or DEMOTED.

## Calibration - CHECKED (all recorded anchors reproduce)

Machine results (`verify.py`, stdlib, deterministic; certificate digest `86f48c1bacdbe4a9`):

| anchor | recorded by | recorded value | this package |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tied_min` one-copy L8 | [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) by DreamingOfClouds (CP-SAT, CHECKED (recorded)) | 11 | 11 (hill-climb re-found, witness replayed) |
| `cex_min_1` one-copy L8 | [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) by DreamingOfClouds (CP-SAT, CHECKED (recorded)) | 18 | 18 (stored witness replayed) |
| chain engine on `cex_min_1` stored pairing | [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) by DreamingOfClouds | 22 (ranks 10 + 6 + 6) | 22 (admissibility re-checked) |
| Lemma MP on `tied_min` | [PR 2747](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2747) by Aaron Wang (navinor) | 9 (4096 pivot maps) | 9 (4096 pivot maps, exhaustive) |
| Lemma MP on `cex_min_1` | [PR 2747](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2747) by Aaron Wang (navinor) | 16 (6144 pivot maps) | 16 (6144 pivot maps, exhaustive) |

## New: the dichromatic structure of the canonical fixtures - CHECKED

| instance | v | `floor(2v/3)` | `chi(Z)` unconstrained | `MAS(Z)` | largest mutual-zero clique | MP (exhaustive) | `v - MP` | 3-dichromatic under `D` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tied_min` | 12 | 8 | 3 exactly (subset DP, exhaustive) | 4 | 3 | 9 | 3 | no |
| `cex_min_1` | 19 | 12 | 3 exactly (colouring found; a mutual-zero triangle forces 3) | 10 | 3 | 16 | 3 | no |

Consequences, each CHECKED:

1. Both canonical fixtures have dichromatic number exactly 3 without the pivot constraints. The obstruction that keeps `cert(M)` below `v` on `cex_min_1` (18 of 19) is therefore not the dichromatic number of the digraph; it lives in the pivot constraint sets `D(t)` together with the labelling structure. PR 2717's open question 2 ("can `Z` itself be non-3-dichromatic") is not realized by either fixture; both fixtures are non-3-dichromatic under `D`, which is the operative sense of class (ii) for Lemma MP.
2. The largest mutual-zero clique is 3 on both fixtures: the Lemma RK (a) bound (no mutual-zero `K_4`) is attained, so clique bounds alone cannot force a dichromatic number above 3 on these instances.
3. The matched-pivot value loses exactly 3 lines on each fixture (9 below 12, 16 below 19), and both values stay at or above both threshold forms (9 versus 8; 16 versus 12 and 13). F-star holds on both canonical class-(ii) instances by the structural certificate alone.

## New: smallest-first falsifier search in the class-(ii) domain - CHECKED (scoped negative)

Smallest falsifying instance first: `v` ascending from 3, four generator families per `v` (entries in `{-1,0,1}` and `{-2..2}`), all aimed at the residue: `random` / `random2` (unstructured boxes), `sparse` (1-2 nonzero coordinates per `p(t)`, `q(t)`, dense zero digraphs), `forced` (support masks chosen first so at least half the lines have `|D(t)| = 1`, heavily constrained pivot maps), `mutual` (rejection sampling for many mutual-zero pairs). 286 instances, `v = 3..12`, deterministic seeds per instance in `CERTIFICATE.json`.

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| falsifiers (explicit admissible `B` with chain cost below `floor(2v/3)`, or exact `cert` below threshold) | 0 |
| instances with matched-pivot value below `floor(2v/3)` | 0 |
| minimum matched-pivot ratio | 2/3 (attained at `v = 3`, seed 4611, matched-pivot value 2 equal to `floor(2v/3)`) |
| minimum engine-witness ratio | 0.909 (10 at `v = 11`; every witness above threshold) |
| instances non-3-dichromatic under `D` (matched-pivot value below `v`) | 8 (listed below) |
| instances with `chi(Z) >= 4` unconstrained | 0 found (286 of 286 backtracking decisions found a 3-colouring; 0 undecided) |

The complete class-(ii) population found (every one has `chi(Z)` at most 3 unconstrained and `cert(M) = v` exactly by exhaustive a-enumeration):

| v | seed | family | MP | `floor(2v/3)` | exact `cert` | arcs in `Z` | mutual-zero pairs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 4611 | random | 2 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 1 |

**Exact obstruction record (early kill).** The matched-pivot value never fell below `floor(2v/3)` anywhere in the domain; its deficit `v - MP` never exceeded 3 (attained only on the fixtures), while the MP route would need the deficit to exceed `ceil(v/3)` (4 at `v = 12`, 7 at `v = 19`) to fail on an instance. The first instance where the matched-pivot value touches the floor exactly (`v = 3`, seed 4611) still has `cert(M) = v` exactly. On all eight class-(ii) instances the general labellings reach `cert(M) = v` while matched pivots do not: label patterns beyond matched pivots (the same effect PR 2747 documented on `tied_min`, matched-pivot 9 versus `cert` 11) carry the certificate there.

## What is proved, what is witnessed, what is demoted

- **PROVEN:** nothing new. This package proves no new lemma; Lemma MP and the chain `cost >= sum_j r_j >= cert(M)` are cited from [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717) by Aaron Wang (navinor) and the merged `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` package ([PR 1590](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1590) by DreamingOfClouds, with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code assistance), not restated.
- **CHECKED (machine, `verify.py`, stdlib, deterministic, about 57 s):** controls (brute-force-over-all-labellings agreement 3/3 at `v = 3`, diagonal decoder `cert = 3`, corrupted-witness rejection 2/2, subset-DP MAS hand values 3/3, dichromatic hand values 4/4, MP 3 on the diagonal decoder); the calibration table above; the dichromatic structure of both fixtures; and the 286-instance search with exact MP values, replayed witnesses, exact `cert` where a-enumeration terminates, and bounded admissible-`B` chain scans.
- **DEMOTED / OPEN:** F-star for general rational decoders is neither proved nor refuted. The matched-pivot floor `max_c sum_i MAS(Z[C_i]) >= floor(2v/3)` is witnessed on 288 instances (2 fixtures plus 286 searched), not proved. No "exactly when" or necessity claim is made for any hypothesis. Whether some rank-3 zero digraph has `chi(Z) >= 4` unconstrained remains open (none found here; the decision is exact when it terminates and no run in this domain was undecided, but the search is bounded in `v`). Chain costs are bounded-search upper bounds on the minimum, not exact minima. The recorded fixture limits 11 and 18 rest on PR 2111's recorded CP-SAT optimality, not re-verified here. Residue classes (i) and (iii) are not re-attacked. One control's expected value was initially written wrong (the dichromatic number of a directed 3-cycle is 2, not 1; the subset DP returned the correct 2) and the control was corrected after the first run; the correction is recorded in the README rather than hidden.

# KB3c: 17-point cover audit — PR 2542's "no 17-point set covers F2^7" against its own lemma table (no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no model named; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the PR943 prefix-walk model ([PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) by Ross Richardson, `research/universal-connector-boundary`), universality of a restored seven-source singleton word is the covering condition `P + P = F2^7` on its prefix set. [PR 2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542) by Aaron Wang (`research/universal-f7-singleton-seedb859517b`) excludes length 18 and asserts in its README: **"No 17-point set covers `F2^7`"**. Its machine-checked `lemma_a_table` contradicts only the parity split rows `(9,8)/(8,9)`, and its certificate records `size17_splits = {"9_8": false, "8_9": false}` only. The counting-feasible 17-point splits `(|E|,|O|)` are exactly `(9,8),(8,9),(10,7),(7,10),(11,6),(6,11)`; the four non-`(9,8)` rows survive the identity as written (`lemma_a_table(7, 10, 7)` is feasible; [PR 2634](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2634) by Aaron Wang already pins that in `test_lemma_rows_survive_at_L20`).

This package audits the claim at the set level and decides the surviving rows exactly:

1. **The pair-representation identity is extended to all six rows** with the sharp collision-multiplicity constraint: cross-sum collisions satisfy `sum_o C(r_o, 2) = 2 sum_x A_x B_x` with odd excess `sum_o (r_o - 1) = s*t - 64`, and `C(r, 2) >= r - 1` per mask turns each excess into an integer collision profile. Rows survive iff a profile's `c` is exactly attainable over the shared support values. `(9,8)/(8,9)` re-killed (best 1, need 4); `(10,7)` forces `c` in `{3,4,5,6,8}` (six rows); `(11,6)` collapses to the single row class `(e_ex, b_ex, c) = (e, 6-e, 1)` with `shared = 1`.
2. **An exact Sidon/near-Sidon census of the even group `E = F2^6`** shows the minimum pair-sum excess of any 10-point set is at least 3 (in particular `F2^6` has no Sidon 10-set), and likewise at least 3 for 11-point sets. Complete shards through `{0, 3}`: 9-sets Sidon `17,776,640`; 10-sets excess `<= 2`: `0`; 11-sets excess `<= 2`: `0`; 7-sets in the odd coset Sidon `34,122,816`. The shard is existence-complete by `GL(6,2)` transitivity and invariance (the extension to the odd coset preserves pair sums, cross sums and coverage).
3. **Result: the `(10,7)/(7,10)` splits are excluded exactly** — after the census floor `e_ex >= 3` the only identity row left attains `c = 0`, which is not a profile value. **`(11,6)/(6,11)` are reduced to four rows** `(3,3),(4,2),(5,1),(6,0)`, each with one shared sum carrying `A_x = B_x = 1`. PR 2542's literal claim is now established for every split its length-18 exclusion needed and for the length-20-relevant splits; the length-22-relevant `(11,6)/(6,11)` rows remain open.

Exact controls validate the machinery: the enumeration agrees with naive brute force on a 16-element subgroup at budgets 0/1/2; `independent.py` re-derives every row by a different code path (direct count-vector loops); the exact `n = 5` set censuses reproduce the community facts (zero nine-point covers, max 29 of 32; `99,200` ten-point covers of all `C(31,9) = 20,160,075` sets); the odd-translation mirror is machine-checked.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, standard library only, Python 3.12:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-17point-cover-audit-seedcfa215c2/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/f7-17point-cover-audit-seedcfa215c2/independent.py
python3 -I -B research/f7-17point-cover-audit-seedcfa215c2/test_engine.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-17point-cover-audit-seedcfa215c2 --check-only
```

Observed markers: `PASS_17POINT_VERIFY seconds=148.5`, `PASS_17POINT_INDEPENDENT {...}`, `Ran 13 tests ... OK`, `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. `verify.py --full` re-runs the four load-bearing zero-count census shards (`~17 min`) and compares them with `SIDON-RECEIPT.json`.

Before any new number the recorded predecessor state is reproduced byte-exactly (vendored engine SHA-256 pinned `82e4c407b58864c7…`, enforced by test): the pinned tiers `945/31`, `10395/49`, `945945/59` with records SHA-256 against `research/universal-connector-six-source/EXPECTED.json`, and PR 2542's decisive length-18 census re-run in full: `15,775,992` nodes, `312,064` simple 18-cycles, zero universal words. In-session runs of PR 2634's own verifier at head `e2f30d93` additionally reproduced its search campaign `120/126/128` at lengths 20/22/24 and its then-partial 20-cycle census (`11/15` shards, `798,901,058` nodes, `67,674,177` cycles). The completed `(10,10)` census is recorded state from [PR 2691](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2691) by Nicholas Stone (`6,305,209,079` nodes, `597,148,314` simple 20-cycles, zero universal, 15/15 shards) and is not re-run here.

## Pair-collision disclosure and object change

This session was assigned KB3c (finish the L=20 census and attack its recorded remainder: the repeated-state splits). The entry pair-collision check found both assigned options claimed or completed: option (a) is completed by [PR 2691](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2691) (Nicholas Stone), and options (b)/(c) are the active claim of Nicholas Stone (Kimi agent) on the repeated-state L=20 **word** census ([discussion 1166 comment 18954844](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18954844)). The object was therefore changed, per the pair-collision rule, to the set-level question the assignment itself names as the recorded remainder: PR 2542's overreaching "no 17-point set" claim. This package enumerates no words. Handoff to the concurrent claim: its `(10,7)/(7,10)` L=20 word splits are empty a fortiori, since a universal word there would yield a 17-point cover of split `(10,7)/(7,10)`, excluded here.

## Scope and limits

A finite set-level audit inside PR943's abstract interface. Not checked: realizability of the four surviving `(11,6)` rows (the joint `(A, B)` tree needs stabilizer canonical forms; the `GL(6,2)`-invariance lemma reduces the domain to `0, 3 in A` but does not canonicalize pairs — this is the open next question of the package README), the 18-/19-point cover question `r((C2)^7)`, and every word-level question. No kappa, supplier, tariff or selected-frontier change; the recorded gap `20 <= f(7) <= 24` is unchanged. Canonical main moved to `1696cf14e403b3eab35cd9eab27a4c2eb4e4ae38` during the session (priority revision 5); the base commit `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` is retained per the assignment pin, and `certificates/selected-result.json` is byte-identical between the two.

## Credit

- [PR 2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542) by Aaron Wang (navinor): the audited claim, the pair-representation identity (`lemma_a_table`), the length-18 exclusion; its `engine.py` is vendored byte-exact with a hash pin.
- [PR 2634](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2634) by Aaron Wang (navinor): the recorded KB3b state, the L=20 campaign and census, and the pinned `(10,7)` identity row.
- [PR 2691](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2691) by Nicholas Stone (NicholasStone, Kimi agent, substantial AI assistance): the completed `(10,10)` simple-20-cycle census and its released independent audit.
- [PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) by Ross Richardson (RossRichardson): the prefix-walk model.
- [PR 1185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185) by Doug Colkitt (Mister-Meeseeks): the pinned record `f(5) = 12`, `f(6) = 16`, `18 <= f(7) <= 24`.

The original PR2041 cover has strict scalar fitting rank 99. This contribution changes the cover of the same 112 selected labels and certifies minimum scalar fitting rank **57**, with explicit factors and a matching identity minor. It then proves why minimizing scalar rank does not produce an affordable decoder under the full port-space tariff:

- **Exactly 57 rational rank-one terms cost at least 334**, over every fitting matrix on this mask. The saved construction attains 334, so this floor is sharp.
- **Every fit with at most 58 nonzero rational terms costs at least 297**, including asymmetric factors, exterior directions that cancel, and fitting matrices of rank 58. This lower bound is not claimed sharp.
- **The sharp minimum is 334 at any factor count** when the fitted matrix has rank 57 and both factor families remain in its column and row spaces. With `m=57+s` nonzero terms, `C >= 334+2s`. This supersedes the earlier valid but weaker 308 lower bound; adding terms inside both spans cannot improve the saved construction.

All three floors exceed the favorable positive-saving allowance `2672/9` (integer charge at most 296). A successful scalar decoder on this mask therefore needs **at least 59 terms**, and must also escape the rank-57/both-spans restriction. Those cases, changed covers and operator contracts remain open. **No cheaper decoder, native supplier, selected-result change or exponent improvement is claimed.**

The minimum-length proof uses the forced identity minor, Schur complement and duality. The sharp any-length/both-spans extension uses the same complete 40-space closure and 272 cheap rectangles. Retaining the identical pure-J count in the full57 and restricted54 acyclic bounds gives `C >=2m-3P+229` and `C >=2m+P+217`; their one-quarter/three-quarter convex combination is `C >=2m+220`. The new 58-term proof handles rank 57 through its one-sided exterior normal form, and rank 58 through a rank-one Schur complement whose support lies in a forest. Exact censuses cover **1,750 physical-triad spans, 2,318 affected-set unions and all 314 nonempty Schur support rectangles**. Singular paired maps, the exceptional 4/24 branch and a possible zero retained source column are handled explicitly. Rational coefficients are not reduced modulo two; binary linear algebra prices group geometry.

See the [sharp canonical-span proof](https://github.com/flyingviper/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18da668a4f248f5c0cf3fc94355068ead4db3476/research/p112-rational-decoder-gate/CANONICAL-SHARP-PROOF.md), [rank-tight proof](https://github.com/flyingviper/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18da668a4f248f5c0cf3fc94355068ead4db3476/research/p112-rational-decoder-gate/RANK-TIGHT-PROOF.md) and [exterior-factor proof](https://github.com/flyingviper/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18da668a4f248f5c0cf3fc94355068ead4db3476/research/p112-rational-decoder-gate/EXTERIOR-58-PROOF.md) for the written arguments. # F-star residue (i): mixed anchor-repair-pivot lemma MX, tied-instance certificates, and a tied-domain search (no kappa)

## Scope

Kappa-blocker **KB5b** (explicit open request; scope changed from the drawn card and recorded in `TASK.json`): residue class **(i) tied-minimum / isotropic lines** of open problem **F-star** of the merged `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` package (section 7): `cert(M) >= floor(2v/3)` for every exact 3-total rational decoder `M = sum_j p_j q_j^T`. This is the exact residue that [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717) (Aaron Wang) left after proving Lemmas SF, MP, RK and AN: lines the mod-2 anchor cannot anchor (tied-minimum / isotropic lines), where Lemma AN handles only the count of odd diagonals and not their repair or ordering. Package `research/fstar-tied-residue-seeddcc97691/`, branch `research/agent-65-fstar-tied-residue-dcc97691`, base main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` (priority revision 4). No kappa, certificate, supplier, window or frontier change. **F-star itself is not proved and not refuted here.**

Agent: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent human review claimed).

## Result 1 — Lemma MX (PROVEN)

A mixed anchor-repair-pivot certificate with exact hypotheses, in two order forms. Anchor labels on a set `A` (lines with `M_tt` odd), one-sided repairs `a*(t)` on a set `U` (with `b` fixed at the anchor's `b0`), matched pivots `a(t) = b(t) = e_{c(t)}` with `c(t)` in `D(t)` on the rest `T`; per pivot class `C_i`, `MAS(Z[C_i])` is the maximum acyclic induced subset of the zero digraph. Then `cert(M) >= |A| + |U| + sum_i MAS(Z[C_i])` under either (a-first) "the repairs kill their `A`/`U` and `T` blockers and no `A`-to-`T` conflict remains", or (t-first) "the repairs kill their `A`/`U` blockers and no `T`-to-`A`/`U` conflict remains". Written proof in the README. Its `U`/`T`-empty special case is Lemma AN of [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717); its `A`/`U`-empty special case is Lemma MP of [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717), so MX subsumes both as sufficient conditions.

## Result 2 — the canonical tied instances are closed by structural certificates (CHECKED)

Per-line residue classification (relative to the stored primitive 2-integral normalization: `anchor_good` = `M_tt` odd; `repairable_1s` = full one-sided repair exists with `b` fixed; `tied_isotropic` = neither), then exhaustive maximization over **all** pivot maps as unit masks (4096 on `tied_min`, 6144 on `cex_min_1`), every accepted value carrying a witness replayed by an independent checker:

| instance | v | floor(2v/3) | ceil(2v/3) | AN | MP (exhaustive) | MX (max) | engine witness | PR 2111 recorded |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| tied_min | 12 | 8 | 8 | 0 | 9 | 9 | 11 (re-found) | 11 (recorded) |
| cex_min_1 | 19 | 12 | 13 | 8 | 16 | 16 | 18 (replayed) | 18 (recorded) |

F-star holds on both canonical tied-minimum instances by a structural certificate (9 and 16, at or above both the floor and the ceiling threshold), even though the mod-2 anchor is vacuous on `tied_min` (0 of 12 lines) and short on `cex_min_1` (8 of 19). Both fixtures are entirely `tied_isotropic` outside the anchor set (0 one-sided repairable), so the residue is total there. The engine witnesses reproduce DreamingOfClouds' recorded one-copy L8 maxima of [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) (their CP-SAT optimality is recorded, not re-verified here).

## Result 3 — exact obstruction to the mixed route (CHECKED)

On `cex_min_1` no anchor/pivot mixture helps in either block order: the a-first separation fails for 6144/6144 pivot maps (`A`-to-`T` conflict) and the t-first separation fails for 6144/6144 (`T`-to-`A`/`U` conflict). The winning value 16 is the pure matched-pivot construction. This is the exact obstruction to extending AN/MP by naive mixing on the canonical hard instance.

## Result 4 — tied-domain falsifier search, smallest first (CHECKED, scoped negative)

40 instances at `v = 3..12` (two per family and `v`), families `tied_isotropic` (every line constructed with two tied minimal valuations at level 0 and even diagonal) and `mixed` (half unique-minimum anchorable, half tied). Zero falsifiers. `cert = v` on all 40: 16 decided by exhaustive `a`-enumeration at `v <= 6`, 24 pinned by full-size replayed witnesses (a witness of size `v` pins `cert = v` exactly). Minimum witness ratio 1.0. The falsifier criterion (explicit admissible pairing `B` with block-rank chain cost below `floor(2v/3)`, which by the proven chain would refute F-star) was tested by an exhaustive `B`-scan up to 12 free pairs and a deterministic local search above: no `B` below threshold on any instance (bounded search, not an exhaustive non-falsification proof). Lemma MP reaches `v` on all 40; Lemma MX is never below MP and never strictly above it on this domain.

## What is proved, witnessed, demoted

- **PROVEN:** Lemma MX, both order forms, exact hypotheses, written proof.
- **CHECKED (stdlib `verify.py`, deterministic, certificate digest `439d75261e9a2b9e`):** controls (brute/engine agreement 3/3 at `v = 3`, diagonal decoder `cert = 3`, corrupted-witness rejection 2/2, MX all-anchor reproducing AN's count, MP control with replayed witness); the fixture classification; the exhaustive MP/MX maxima 9/16 with replayed witnesses; the 6144/6144 obstruction counts in both forms; engine witnesses 11/18; the 40-instance search (`cert = v` on all, zero falsifiers).
- **DEMOTED:** F-star for general rational decoders is not proved. That matched pivots always reach `floor(2v/3)` is witnessed on 42 instances, not proved. No hypothesis is claimed necessary. Residue classes (ii) (non-3-dichromatic zero digraphs) and (iii) (non-dyadic entries) are untouched. `B`-scan values are bounded-search upper bounds on the minimum chain cost. The fixture certificates 11/18 rest on [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111)'s recorded CP-SAT optimality. Exact pairing costs elsewhere (12 on `tied_min`, [PR 2379](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2379) by Aaron Wang; 21 on `cex_min_1`, [PR 2206](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2206) by Nick Petalas) are cited, not recomputed.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/fstar-tied-residue-seeddcc97691/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/fstar-tied-residue-seeddcc97691 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/fstar-tied-residue-seeddcc97691
```

Expected: `PASS_FSTARTIED_CONTROLS`, `PASS_FSTARTIED_FIXTURES`, `PASS_FSTARTIED_MX`, `PASS_FSTARTIED_SEARCH`, `PASS_FSTAR_TIED_RESIDUE`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/fstar-tied-residue-seeddcc97691 outcome=completed` (registered replay: 378.81 s, under the 600 s manifest cap). `make` is not installed on the authoring host.

## Credit

F-star, `cert(M)`, L8 labellings and the proven chain: merged `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` ([PR 1590](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1590) by DreamingOfClouds, with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code assistance). Fixtures `tied_min`/`cex_min_1`, their recorded certificate limits and the stored cost-22 pairing: DreamingOfClouds, [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) and [PR 2162](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162). The residue statement, Lemmas SF/MP/RK/AN and the engine design this adapts: Aaron Wang, [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717). The falsifier-census frontier: Aaron Wang, [PR 2335](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2335). Exact cost 12 of `tied_min`: Aaron Wang, [PR 2379](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2379). Exact cost 21 of `cex_min_1`: Nick Petalas, [PR 2206](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2206). New work here is Lemma MX with its proof, the residue classification, the mixed-route obstruction and the tied-domain search.

**Open next questions** are in the package README: (1) does the matched-pivot family always reach `floor(2v/3)` (which would prove F-star)? (2) does insertion-finite mixing (per-anchor-line cuts of the pivot order) survive the 6144/6144 obstruction? (3) which label patterns do the attaining certificates 11 and 18 actually use?

**Status: research note with an exact finite enumeration (not a SAT/DRAT proof). No κ claim, no supplier word.** Only `research/nine-term-outside-colspace/` is added; nothing existing is changed.

## What this proves (scope is the claim)

Model of #2338 / #2277 / #1224: `N = Σ_{j≤m} p_j q_jᵀ` exact for the masked P112 / P104 pattern (zero on orthogonal pairs, nonzero diagonal), arbitrary factors over a field of characteristic 0, cost `Σ_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j]`.

* **P112: cost ≥ 64** and **P104 (#968's unit, `F1 = H4`, only): cost ≥ 56** for every decoder with **`m = 9`**, a **rank-8 realisation** (`rank N = 8`), and **exactly one factor outside `col M`** ("case (b)" of #2338's `m = 9` trichotomy; the one-sided nine-term decoders of #1224), **dense `B`**, hence every fitting `B` of F2-rank ≤ 9 (Theorem R of #2338).
* The result relies on #2338 (our own PR, open and ready): Theorem P, Theorem R, and "≤ 8 paid terms ⇒ ≥ 64 / ≥ 56".
* Realisation-free: only the support-propagation lemma (valid in every rank-8 realisation) and the reductions are used; the rigidity PRs (#1212, #1815) are not needed.
* Method: the lift `κ` of the outside factor is free (Lemma 2.1, PROVEN), which reduces the cost count to exact class-level accounting `Σσ_j ≥ 9` over the 511 label classes. Exact enumeration: no big term (counting); ≥ 2 big terms (41 configurations → 0 on P112, 701 → 0 on P104); one big term with row deficiency `d₀ = 2, …, 8` (residues 8, 1, 17, 0, 0, 0, 0, all killed by the support filter).

## Not covered (stated up front)

* **Case (c): square decoders of a RANK-9 realisation.** This contains every nine-term masked **co-star** decoder (D1267, philippeVV; #2338 shows these are case (c)) and the A2 family. Nothing here bears on the co-star programme.
* `m ≥ 10` (one- and two-sided); `B` of rank ≥ 10; other punctured units.
* Not DRAT-logged: the enumeration is exact Python on finite data, re-runnable, but not proof-checked by a solver.

## Labels (every step is in the README)

PROVEN: Lemma 2.1 (free lift), the accounting `Σσ_j ≥ 9`, the "no big term" case, the `d₀ = 7, 8` reduction. CHECKED (exact enumeration): the ≥ 2-big census, `d₀ = 2, 3, 4, 7, 8`, all of P104. **CHECKED-INDEPENDENTLY** (separate re-implementation by a different session, exact agreement): `d₀ = 5, 6` only (`evidence/helper/`). **Not independently re-implemented:** `d₀ = 2, 3, 4, 7, 8`, the ≥ 2-big census, P104. A separate reviewer run found one incompleteness (repeated extra classes were forbidden), fixed in `cnt7/8/9`, everything re-run, residues unchanged. The exact-rank formula (IDEAL Thm 3 / BIGTHEORY Thm A) is proved in the README (3 lines) and spot-checked on 2,974 + 2,973 random blocks, 0 mismatches; the reductions (free-term absorption, merge lemma) are inlined; the geometric inputs (frames, survivors, survivor-pair ranks, 7-cliques) are re-computed by `checks/inputs_check.py`.

## Verification

`bash research/nine-term-outside-colspace/verify.sh /fresh/dir` (Python ≥ 3.11, `numpy`, `networkx`; one core; no SAT). On a fresh `git archive` export (default mode, single process, venv Python 3.14, numpy 2.5, networkx 3.7, on a heavily loaded machine): **92 PASS, 0 FAIL**, 839 s wall (12.0 min user CPU).

**What `verify.sh` re-runs:** the geometric inputs on both units; the exact-rank formula spot check; regeneration of orbits / cliques / pair census; exact line-for-line replay (vs. the recorded logs) of `cnt4` (`d₀ = 2, 3`), `cnt7`/`cnt8` for `d₀ = 2, 3, 7, 8`; subset replays of the census (P112 orbits 8, 13; P104 orbits 9, 30, 56); `cnt9` / `cnt9b` from the recorded compact census output; the two controls (`ctl8`, `ctlb`).

The full chain re-runs with `FULL=1` (hours; not run for the transcript). The shipped logs and data are pinned in `MANIFEST.sha256`.

# F-star proof-level lemmas: structural certificates, named-instance L8 reproduction, and a beyond-census falsifier search (no kappa)

## Scope

Kappa-blocker **KB5** (explicit open request; scope changed from the drawn card and recorded in `TASK.json`): proof-level work on open problem **F-star** of the merged `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` package (section 7, OPEN): `cert(M) >= floor(2v/3)` for every exact 3-total rational decoder `M = sum_j p_j q_j^T` on `v` lines. Package `research/fstar-proof-lemmas-seed3096ed3f/`, branch `research/agent-63-fstar-proof-3096ed3f`, head `10644c90`, base main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` (priority revision 4). No kappa, certificate, supplier, window or frontier change.

The predecessor https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2335 established a census over 196 declared instances with machine-checked witnesses at or above `floor(2v/3)` and no falsifier, and stated explicitly that witnesses are lower bounds on `cert`, not a proof. This session moves toward proof level along three tracks: written structural lemmas with exact hypotheses, an independent reproduction of the named-instance certificates of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111, and a targeted falsifier search beyond the censused domain. **F-star itself is not proved and not refuted here;** the residue is stated exactly below.

## Proven lemmas (proofs in the package README)

- **Lemma SF (support-forced incidences vanish).** `K_ts = 0` whenever `pi(t) intersect sigma(s)` is empty, for every L8 labelling; so the conflict digraph lies inside the block-incidence digraph `H` and `cert(M) >= MAS(H)`, `cert(M) = v` when `H` is acyclic, `cert(M) >= v - fvs(H)`.
- **Lemma MP (matched-pivot certificate).** For every pivot map `c(t)` into `D(t) = pi(t) intersect sigma(t)`, `cert(M) >= sum_i MAS(Z[C_i])` over the three pivot classes; hence `cert(M) = v` whenever the zero digraph `Z` is 3-dichromatic with pivots inside `D(t)`.
- **Lemma RK (rank-3 structural facts).** The mutual-zero graph has no `K_4`; `Z` contains no transitive 4-tournament; an incidence with `|pi(t) intersect sigma(s)| = 1` is impossible.
- **Lemma AN (mod-2 anchor).** For 2-integral (dyadic) factorizations, the mod-2 reduction of the factors is an L8 labelling with `K_ts = 0` at every incidence and `K_tt = M_tt mod 2`; so `cert(M) >= #{t : M_tt odd}` and **F-star holds for dyadic decoders with at most `floor(v/3)` even diagonals**.

Each lemma is a sufficient condition stated exactly; none is claimed necessary. The anchor leaves the tied-minimum (isotropic) lines of the source package's section 7 obstruction uncovered; a structure theorem for them remains the open core.

## Checked results (verify.py, stdlib, deterministic, 12 s registered replay)

- **Named-instance L8 certificates reproduced by a different method.** Exact-completion engine plus independent witness replay, from byte-identical copies of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111 data files:

| instance | v | [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) recorded max one-copy L8 | this package | threshold floor(2v/3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tied_min | 12 | 11 | 11, machine-checked and re-found by the deterministic search | 8 |
| cex_min_1 | 19 | 18 | 18, stored witness replayed | 12 |

- **Chain engine validated on real data.** [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111)'s stored pairing for `cex_min_1` is recomputed as exactly 22 (ranks 10+6+6) and confirmed admissible.
- **Exact cert values** by exhaustive a-enumeration with exact completion: two `v = 5` instances and one `v = 6` instance, each `cert = v` exactly (upgrades the census's witness-level claims to exact values on their instances).
- **Structural lemma checks** on 45 instances: mutual-zero `K_4`-freeness and no transitive 4-tournament on 44 with `v <= 16`, matched-pivot witness from `MAS(H)` replayed on 28 with `v <= 12`.
- **Beyond-census falsifier search** (smallest falsifying instance first): 43 instances — factor entries `{-3..3}` at `v = 4..12` (27 instances, outside the census alphabet `{-2..2}`), `v = 13..16` with entries `{-3..3}` (8), and `v = 13..16` tied-heavy 2-adic constructions (8, outside the census `v`-range and deliberately accumulating the named isotropic obstruction). Falsifier criterion: an explicit admissible pairing `B` with `sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j,A_j] < floor(2v/3)`, which the proven chain turns into `cert(M) < floor(2v/3)`. **Zero falsifiers**; minimum witness ratio 0.867 (13/15 at `v = 15` against threshold 10), every witness replayed by the independent checker. The `B`-search is a bounded deterministic search, so its chain numbers are labelled upper bounds; a missing low-cost `B` cannot create a false falsifier, but the search is not an exhaustive non-falsification proof.

Controls (all required to pass): brute-force-over-all-labellings agreement with the engine on three tiny instances (3/3), the hand-checkable diagonal decoder at `cert = 3`, corrupted-witness rejection (2/2), the threshold table, and the proven chain rechecked per instance. Markers: `PASS_FSTAR_CONTROLS`, `PASS_FSTAR_NAMED`, `PASS_FSTAR_CHAIN_ENGINE`, `PASS_FSTAR_EXACT`, `PASS_FSTAR_STRUCTURAL`, `PASS_FSTAR_SEARCH`, `PASS_FSTAR_PROOF_LEMMAS`; certificate digest `134665ac6a0800e4`.

## What is demoted

F-star for general rational decoders stays **OPEN**. The exact residue: (a) lines no 2-integral normalization anchors odd (the tied-minima obstruction), whose repair or mutual ordering is unresolved; (b) zero digraphs that are not 3-dichromatic, where Lemma MP gives only the class sum; (c) non-dyadic entries (odd primes in denominators), where the mod-2 anchor does not apply. No exactly-when or necessity wording is used for any hypothesis. The `tied_min` and `cex_min_1` equalities at 11 and 18 rely on [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111)'s recorded CP-SAT optimality, which this package does not independently re-verify; only the certificate sides (11 and 18 are attainable and match) are reproduced here.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, Python 3.10+, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -B research/fstar-proof-lemmas-seed3096ed3f/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/fstar-proof-lemmas-seed3096ed3f --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/fstar-proof-lemmas-seed3096ed3f
```

The registered CPython 3.12 replay prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/fstar-proof-lemmas-seed3096ed3f outcome=completed`. `make` is not installed on the authoring host; the commands above are the underlying ones.

## Credit and overlap

F-star, the `cert(M)` definition, L8 labellings and the proven chain `cost >= sum_j r_j >= cert(M)` are from the merged `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` package (Douglas Colkitt with OpenAI Codex assistance lineage). The rank-3 configuration model, the named instances `tied_min` and `cex_min_1`, their recorded certificate limits (11 and 18), the stored cost-22 pairing, Lemma SCC's block-incidence digraph and L5 are DreamingOfClouds' work in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162. The census this builds on is https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2335 (same author line). Refined overlap passes at entry and before computation (proper names: F-star, cert, 3-total decoder, labelling, root-unit decoder, floor(2v/3), tied-min; complete pagination over 827 open PRs and 1292 discussion records) found no other proof-level F-star work; the board claim is https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18954341.

Prepared by **Aaron Wang** with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent human review claimed). New work is Apache-2.0; all pinned sources and licenses are retained.

## Summary

Conditional κ = **0.0017148565406944333620724957866041817002…** (exact `kappa` in `research/gmx-t74-borrow43-handoff/outer/OUTER-CLAIM.json`; κ = C − 10⁻³⁰⁴⁶ − 10⁻³⁰²², with C the certified 10⁻³⁰⁰⁰ complex endpoint). This exceeds #2588 (jeremykothe2, 0.001714252039260245…) by **+6.045e-7** (≈0.035%), and #2673 (0.001714600409398252) by +2.56e-7. Built on #2588's head 8cd9dc88. The exact gates are in `verify_release.py`.

**New mechanism: pre-life hosting.** After a cold width-4 helper h has restored itself and retired, it hosts the entire life of a later width-9 helper L that starts at dimension 0.
- One B warp carries h's cold-end frame onto a dim-4 frame E at L's first gate.
- L's dirt-compensation reads become anticipatory corrections t += c·K_op(h), pulled back through the target-only precondition.
- h stops being cold, so its zero buffer is freed.
- Six hostings are used: 482←273, 483←275, 494←289, 495←291, 507←305, 519←321. This is the only admissible form of "gap borrowing" we found. Live-lender gaps fail, because B-phase warp records cannot be undone before cleanup.

**Frame-refit alias.** Gate B894 (`add 515 += 563`) is lowered from dimension 6 to dimension 5. That is its exact propagated floor. The lowering makes the retired-lender alias 653←563 legal.
- A refit census finds 48 refit-OK pairs and no fixed-frame ones.
- Only 653←563 pays. The width-5 followers lose money, because their freed width becomes isolated rank-5 idle.

**Fill.** We used an LNS/evacuation fill on the stacked words. Their certified packing ceiling is C ≤ 0.00171514043461; the bound is an interval-arithmetic LP dual plus a lattice-index tightening, shipped as search-side evidence. | Q | R | X | Tariff |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 (endpoint) | 96 | 8 | **436** |

# KB3b: seven-source singleton `f(7)` continued — parity closes L=19, beating templates closed, cover/walk dichotomy, resumable 20-cycle census

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no model named; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the [PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) prefix-walk model ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943), `research/universal-connector-boundary`), a restored source word `w` over seven singleton labels is universal when paired readouts realize every mask, `D(w) = {q_s xor q_t} = F2^7`, and `f(n)` is the minimum word length. The pinned record ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185), `research/universal-connector-six-source`) left `18 <= f(7) <= 24`; the predecessor of this package removed 18 ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542), `f(7) >= 20`), so the recorded gap is `20 <= f(7) <= 24` with the Gray bound 24 attained. This package (kappa-blocker KB3b, a scoped continuation) advances the next step and reports:

1. **Length 19 is closed exactly, for a structural reason.** Every restored word has even length (all label counts even and at least 2; the cube is bipartite and walks are closed), so no odd length exists to census. The assignment's literal "exclude length 19" is discharged by [PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943)'s restoration facts, and the census step-up from 18 is `L = 20`.
2. **Two natural Gray-beating templates are impossible** (proved lemmas, machine spot-checked): a single-excursion square-detour word `[6, i, j, i, j, 6]` plus a 16-cycle forces its cycle set `R` to be a transversal of the coordinate square, but a transversal's induced-cube graph has the level-set components of its offset map `g`, so a closed walk through `R` needs `g` constant — which makes `R + R` a 16-point plane and misses 48 masks. No word of that template is universal at any length.
3. **20-point covers of `F2^7` exist** (explicit verified example; set-ILS finds covers in 14 of 30 restarts at `k = 20`, 28 of 30 at `k = 22`) — answering part of the predecessor's open question 2 in the direction `r((C2)^7) <= 20`. But every cover sampled (175 at `k = 20` and 288 at `k = 22` in session sweeps, plus the deterministic campaign) has an isolated hypercube vertex, hence admits no closed walk at any length. Covers and walk-shaped sets look disjoint at `k <= 22`; this is quantified evidence, not an exclusion.
4. **A deterministic search campaign with an `L = 24` non-vacuity control** tops out at 120/128 (length 20) and 126/128 (length 22), and finds 128/128 at length 24 in the same optimizer. Extended 600-restart runs confirm both ceilings. These are search failures, not exclusions; they agree with the pinned package's heuristic record (126/128 at length 22).
5. **A resumable restricted-growth simple-20-cycle census** (the `|P| = 20`, `(10,10)` split of `L = 20`, PR 2542's proved-necessary prunes and the split-identity budget `e_ex + b_ex <= 27`) runs with exact per-shard node counts checkpointed in `CENSUS20-PROGRESS.json`. At submission 11 of 15 shards are complete: 798,901,058 nodes and 67,674,177 simple 20-cycles checked, zero universal words (the completed heavy shard `0102` alone accounts for 798,901,031 nodes and 67,674,177 cycles; the small shards die instantly on the self-avoidance prune). The three remaining heavy subtrees are of the same order — a capped probe of `0123` passes 5,000,000 nodes in 21.4 s (234,169 nodes/s) — so completing the `(10,10)` exclusion needs several more hours of the same exact enumeration; the checkpoint is resumable. No universal word appears in the 67.7 million cycles checked so far.

The gap `20 <= f(7) <= 24` is unchanged. The alphabet is singletons only; the charged DUO pair-source family ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2396](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2396), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2128](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2128), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2156](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2156)) and the 63-mask weight-1/2/3 sparse family ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2229](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2229), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2236](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2236), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2397](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2397)) are distinct scopes, recorded as concurrent.

## Method: smallest falsifying instance first

Before any new number, the package reproduces the pinned `research/universal-connector-six-source/EXPECTED.json` byte-for-byte (histograms and records SHA-256 included): 945 words max 31/32 at `n = 5`, length 10 (`3dcc5689…`); 10,395 words max 49/64 at `n = 6`, length 12 (`491b295f…`); 945,945 words max 59/64 at `n = 6`, length 14 (`3d711ffa…`); plus the counting lower bounds 10/14/18 and the Gray constructions 12/16/24. It then fully re-runs the predecessor's decisive length-18 census against its vendored byte-pinned engine and reproduces 15,775,992 nodes, 312,064 simple 18-cycles, zero universal words. Nothing above is taken on trust.

## Reproduction and checks

From the repository root, standard library only, Python 3.12:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-l20-seed06704c39/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-l20-seed06704c39/independent.py
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-l20-seed06704c39/test_engine.py
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-l20-seed06704c39/census20.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/universal-f7-singleton-l20-seed06704c39 --check-only
```

Observed markers:

```text
PASS_F7_L20_VERIFY <conclusion> L20=120 L22=126 seconds=...
PASS_F7_L20_INDEPENDENT {"cover20": "size=20 min_degree=0 no_closed_walk", ...}
Ran 14 tests in 0.040s — OK
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
```

`independent.py` re-checks coverage with three formulations (dual predicate, interval XOR, position pairs) and re-derives the parity fact and the covers' degree obstructions with independently written loops. `test_engine.py` pins the vendored engine byte-exactly (SHA-256 `82e4c407…`), checks the transversal level-set lemma on a deterministic sample, and confirms the deterministic set-ILS hit. The search campaign (`search.py`) is deterministic (fixed CPython `random` seeds); `search.py --extended` runs the 600-restart session budget recorded in `CERTIFICATE.json`.

## Scope and open questions

A finite study inside [PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943)'s abstract interface; no supplier instantiation and no kappa claim. Not checked: the repeated-state `L = 20` splits (`(10,9)`, `(10,8)`, `(9,9)`, `(10,7)` — note the identity kills only the 17-point splits `(9,8)`/`(8,9)`, so `|P| = 17` walks remain open), the `L = 22` census splits, and set-level exhaustive enumeration. Structured next questions are in `TASK.json` and the package README: extend the census to the repeated-state splits with per-split budgets; decide `r((C2)^7) = 20` or lower; and settle whether covers and walk-shape are incompatible at `k <= 22` (which would make the Gray bound 24 sharp).

## Credit

[PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) model and first exact values: Ross Richardson (`research/universal-connector-boundary`). Pinned five/six-source record, counting bounds and Gray constructions: Douglas Colkitt (`research/universal-connector-six-source`, [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185)). Length-18 exclusion, the restricted-growth cycle census engine (vendored here byte-exact with hash pin and credit in `NOTICE.md`/`SOURCES.json`), and the pair-representation identity: Aaron Wang with help from opencode ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542)). The community nine-point five-bit census fact used as a control there is published at [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18931315](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18931315).
