**Update: current selected word (#741).** Rebased on main after #741 merged. I gave CP-SAT PR699's SW4 word (`d232183f…`), using the admissible model with the audit's hpe cone caps and fixed tail frames. In 27 s it returned `OPTIMAL` with exactly #741's profile `{1:2556,2:334,3:430,4:194,5:56,8:8}`, so the solver rediscovers #741's gain without guidance. `check_sw4.py` applies #741's recipe and reproduces its pinned output hash `e7804702…`. The LP optimum over all frame assignments then equals #741's weight: 18155.950422 linear and 18219.665540 exact-root at #741's complex root, with gaps under 1e-9. So **no frame-only change of the selected word can raise κ**; PR699's frame slack (6.90 units) is exactly what #741 recovered. Six commuting-reorder restarts on #741, each re-solved by the LP, gave no gain. The receipt is `RESULT-SW4.json`. This work does not touch the R420/R439 bit or E8 lines (#789/#790/#792, #765/#767/#770).

**Negative result, scoped. No κ change.** By Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani), with substantial AI assistance (an AI coding agent wrote the search code and ran the experiments).

The complex side binds the selected κ. In the 64 jp8 calls, unit climbs make up 160,768 of the 181,659 rank-1 children. Paid children are exactly the frame climbs that `hpe_audit_and_transport.py::climb` counts, and the scalar program never reads frames. So I treated every A/B/tail gate frame of the selected provider words as a variable and searched all of them exactly.

**Result.** For #626's `jp8` and `ck` words (content hashes pinned in `complex-k492-owner-repair/data/SPEC.json`, rebuilt fresh by the package's `verify.py`), the paid profile is optimal over every frame assignment of the fixed gate sequence:

| word | gates | input weight | LP optimum (HiGHS) | CP-SAT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| jp8 | 4471 | 18475.029780700 | 18475.029780701 | OPTIMAL, same value |
| ck | 4507 | 18568.580702034 | 18568.580702035 | OPTIMAL, same value |

The weight is the linearised moment, Σ d·ln(48/d). Each word's rank mass is fixed by its widths, so at the selected root a* the exact criterion is Σ d·(73/d)^a*. That weight is also LP-optimal at the input (gap below 1e-9). The model relaxes the audit: it omits the hpe cone caps and cold_end conditions and leaves tail frames free. So no frame regroup, coalescence or promotion recipe of any size can raise κ on these words. Lifting every frame to its greatest feasible value costs +3.8%. Annealing over commuting reorders (the `build_gate_moves.py` rule), followed by an exact frame re-solve, gave no gain in 11 restarts (`ORDER-SEARCH.json`). That is a sample, not a proof for all orders.

**Context for κ > 0.01.** Jensen's inequality gives a ≤ −ln p / E_mass[ln(73/r)]. At the current deficit (2560 / 523264), a ≥ 0.01 needs a mass-weighted geometric-mean child rank of at least 44.7; today it is 3.66. At today's child ranks it would instead need a deficit of at least 15,425 (6.0×). Reaching it needs new scalar structure, not frame bookkeeping. About 1,700 of jp8's 2,512 rank-1 climbs are helper unit climbs.

**No κ claim.** These are research notes on the E8 unit geometry and on supplier and outer levers. Everything is in `research/e8-decoder-floors-and-cold14-notes/`: one `README.md` with 16 sections, plus a package per section. Each package has its scripts and logs, and most have a `verify.sh` with expected outputs. SAT results have no proof logs unless stated otherwise.

## Headline results

**Gaussian E8 is nearly closed as an E8 replacement.** The unit is E8 over ℤ[i]: 60 lines, window 4. A decoder that beats real E8 needs Theorem-C cost ≤ 42. Proven:
- every decoder costs ≥ 40, and ≥ max(40, 60 − c) for c totals (§10, §15);
- c = 15 costs exactly 60 (§13);
- c ≤ 18 is excluded (§14, §15);
- c = 19 is excluded (§16, MIP bounds).

What remains is **20 ≤ c ≤ 42**: c = 20 is partly done, and c ≥ 21 has an F2 2×2-support route.

**The other E8 replacements lose to E8.**
- Eisenstein (Witting, 40 lines) and Hurwitz E8 cost ≥ v over every decoder (§10).
- Real ADE systems other than E8, the triple family, Lorentzian I_{11,1}/I_{13,1} and K12 have higher ceilings in some cases, but lose once helper costs are counted (§1, §4, §5, §7).

**E8's own decoder floors are tight.** Theorem C equals the star floor: 72 / 63 / 64 for P120 / P111 / P112. The P111 decoder is unique, and deeper punctures, mixed ports and asymmetric sinks are all worse (§2).

**"No new kappa" construction savings cannot move κ.** κ depends only on the paid rank profile and the live stock; ADD and primitive counts enter only slack admission checks (§8).

**Supplier local-edit searches are exhausted on recent words:**
- fusions and triangle slots on the X54 words (§9);
- helper-donor cold kernels on #1319 (§11);
- an extended census on the 566 + 554 T74 word, which also explains why §11 missed those kernels (§12).

## Section index
| § | Topic | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Real ADE root systems as units | only E8 viable (E6 row corrected, per #630) |
| 2 | E8 decoder floors | Theorem C = star (72/63/64); P111 unique; no cheaper variants |
| 3 | #615/#617 levers | e2 ends infeasible; owner map LP-optimal (historical) |
| 4 | E8 over ℤ[i], ℤ[ω], Hurwitz; K12 | minrank = v/w, so x = 1 under the star premise |

| 6 | Dispatch and cold-end pricing (#639 lineage) | ck removal +1.08e-7 b; dim-7 factored ends positive |
| 7 | I_{11,1} / I_{13,1} punctures and helpers | no improving puncture; no 4-frame partition |
| 8 | Why "no new kappa" savings are zero | κ = f(paid profile, W) |
| 9 | Fusion and slot search on the fused X54 words | 0 gains; idle-overlay PRs noted as withdrawn |
| 10 | Extension-ring floors over all decoders | Eisenstein and Hurwitz excluded; Gaussian ≥ 40 |
| 11 | Cold-kernel census on the #1319 word | 0 gains (scope limited, see §12) |

# Prepared binary parameters with a real-ceiling identity

This package adds four unchanged accepted Lean sources. `BinaryPreparedParameters.lean` supplies the actual forty-eight-state, eight-tape composition of the previously published preparation/compact-count and binary-parameter machines. `BinaryCeilLogNatBinding.lean`, `BinaryCeilLogRealBinding.lean` and `BinaryPreparedParametersRealBinding.lean` reuse installed logarithm APIs and attach their identities to that same execution. Twenty public predecessor sources retain their immutable origins; none is republished here.

## Entry, full endpoint and time bound

Let x and y be arbitrary finite Boolean operand words, n=max(x.length,y.length), w=widthBits x y, m=w.length and b=ceilLog2 n. Bits are little-endian under the explicit model's wordValue. Entry is canonical Tape.ofWord x on slot0, Tape.ofWord y on slot1, and pristine Tape.blank on slots2 through7. No arbitrary initial work-tape contents are admitted.

The machine starts in state0. The accepted six-tape prepared compact count runs on slots0 through5; one actual halt-interception transition then runs the accepted three-tape binary-parameter machine on slots5 through7. Slots0 through4 are preserved during this second phase with their actual first-phase endpoint footprints. They are not asserted to remain equal to their original entry tapes.

At some elapsed t<=22*n+13*m+24<=35*n+24 the machine reaches the exact finalConfiguration x y, halted in state47. These are existential elapsed upper bounds, not a first-completion or exact elapsed-count claim.

Write L=leftPad x y and R=rightPad x y for the accepted equal-length zero-padded operand lists, and r=parameterBits x y. Using <left,head,right> for the explicit finite tape, the complete final slots are:

- Slot0: BinaryWordReversal.finalInput L.
- Slot1: BinaryWordReversal.finalInput R.
- Slot2: <L.map bitSymbol ++ [blank],blank,[]>.
- Slot3: <R.map bitSymbol,blank,[]>.
- Slot4: <[],blank,w.map bitSymbol ++ replicate (n-m+1) blank>.
- Slot5: <w.reverse.map bitSymbol,blank,[]>.
- Slot6: <(replicate b false).reverse.map bitSymbol ++ [blank],blank,[]>.
- Slot7: <[],blank,r.map bitSymbol ++ [blank]>.

The reversal's finalInput definition fixes the represented boundary cells on slots0/1; no quotient by trailing blanks is used. The normalized n record w has value n, is empty when n=0, and otherwise has length n.log2+1. Its length is at most n. In the final configuration its head has been scanned to the right blank on slot5. The parameter record r has both length b and value b. It is a marked-home width-b binary record, not a compact binary-b output. Both its home and end blanks are represented, including b=0. The retained slot4 footprint is not shrunk by clearing cells.

For x=y=[], w=[] and r=[]. Visited blanks on the other tapes are retained exactly by the endpoint definitions; this is not a claim that all eight tapes are canonical blanks. Width one also gives b=0. No singleton-zero word is introduced.

The published PR570 token theorem already supplies the least-power characterization. The new Nat adapter reuses the installed Mathlib theorem to identify tokenCount(compact bits) with Nat.clog 2 (wordValue bits), without a new logarithm induction or numeric hypothesis.

The Real adapter then reuses Real.natCeil_logb_natCast. For every width n, the stored b equals the natural ceiling of Real.logb (2 : Nat) (n : Real), under the library's explicit zero extension. For 0<n, the stored b cast to Int equals the integer ceiling of that same real logarithm. Zero and one are explicitly recorded as b=0. At powers of two the exact exponent is used; positive binary length is not substituted for the ceiling.

The final two run theorems conjoin the exact existing physical endpoint and t<=35*n+24 with, respectively, the totalized natural-ceiling identity or the integer-ceiling identity under the explicit premise 0<n. The three adapter sources do not alter the machine, entry, endpoint, assumptions on work tapes, or time bound. # A binary ceiling-log parameter on explicit tapes

This package adds two unchanged accepted Lean sources, `BinaryCeilLogTokens.lean` and `BinaryParameterCount.lean`. A five-state, two-tape machine scans a binary word into zero tokens. A concrete fifteen-state, three-tape machine then counts those tokens into an actual binary record. On normalized input the stored number is the least natural exponent whose power of two bounds the represented value. Fourteen external sources retain their immutable PR origins.

## Exact physical and numeric contracts

For an arbitrary finite Boolean word w, let m=w.length and

b=w.dropLast.length + indicator(w.dropLast.any id).

The token machine starts with canonical Tape.ofWord w and one pristine blank tape. In exactly m+1 elapsed transitions it reaches halted state 4 with input <w.reverse.map bitSymbol,blank,[]> and token tape <replicate b zero,blank,[]>. The output head is at the represented right blank. This exact elapsed identity does not assert first completion.

The binary-parameter machine starts with canonical Tape.ofWord w on slot 0 and pristine Tape.blank on slots 1 and 2. One actual tape-preserving bridge joins the scan to the unchanged automatic-width counter. At some t<=13m+6 it reaches halted state 14. Let u=replicate b false and r=(CarryTape.pass b (replicate b false)).1. The complete final tapes are:

- Slot 0: <w.reverse.map bitSymbol,blank,[]>.
- Slot 1: <u.reverse.map bitSymbol ++ [blank],blank,[]>.
- Slot 2: <[],blank,r.map bitSymbol ++ [blank]>.

The counter bits satisfy r.length=b and wordValue r=b. This is a marked width-b binary record with the head at its home blank, not a canonical compact representation of b. The source ends at its right blank; the token tape also ends at its right blank, retaining the additional represented left blank. The record's home and end blanks are distinct represented cells, including b=0. The theorem gives an existential elapsed upper bound; no first-halting-time claim is made.

Numeric identification uses w=compact bits and v=wordValue bits. The accepted facts identify the stored value with ceilLog2 v and prove, for every natural k,

b<=k if and only if v<=2^k.

The explicit definition is ceilLog2 0=0; for positive v it is v.log2 plus zero when v=2^(v.log2), and one otherwise. Thus zero and one produce b=0, powers of two have their exact exponent, and other positive values use the next exponent. Positive canonical bit length is not silently substituted for this ceiling parameter. The physical theorems hold for arbitrary words; the ceiling identification is only for normalized input. For example the noncanonical word [false,false] emits one token although its numeric value is zero.

For empty input, slot 0 remains the canonical blank, while slot 1 is <[blank],blank,[]> and slot 2 is <[],blank,[blank]>. A normalized one also produces the width-zero marked record. No singleton-zero output encoding is introduced.

Method and knowledge package on the R715 bit word (PR #463): **what sets the width of a residual, how many narrow residuals the shared-donor kernel can give on the retimed R715 word with coordinate entrances (the verified residual-isometry format: exactly 112), and a 112-pivot kernel selection by seeded annealing.** Conditional **κ = 1294233365881801/1000000000000000000 ≈ 1.294233365881801·10⁻³, bit-bound**: +0.838% over #463
and +0.165% over #472 (κ = 1.292099559·10⁻³). It is below the current lemma-less frontier: −0.108% vs #473 (κ = 1.295630·10⁻³, as updated on Oct 11, now the frontier) and −0.098% vs #478 (1.295509·10⁻³). This PR's point is the method and the bounds, not the frontier. The bit supplier is c = 1295910576589222380953/10²⁴ ≈ 1.295911·10⁻³ (+0.839% over R715). Same word, same
hosting rule, same mixing, #458's complex supplier unchanged: only the kernel selection changes, 84 → 112 pivots.

| side | supplier | endpoint |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| bit (binds) | R715 word, **112 rank-1 kernel pivots**, eleven stages, #442 whole-residual hosting, target mixing | c ≈ 1.295911·10⁻³ |
| complex | #458 paid-adapter kernel, unchanged | b ≈ 1.297204·10⁻³ |

**What is new**
1. **The width rule, checked exactly.** A residual's width is 8 − entrance rank, and only kernel pivots have a nonzero entrance: the helper hierarchy and the
   target mixing do not set it. Checked three ways on all 715 helpers (kernel-word frames, exported records of the mixed word, the independent hosted audit).
2. **The pivot ceiling and the exact maximum, for coordinate entrances** (the verified residual-isometry format). A pivot needs a frame line inside its first frame (263 of 706 helpers), and its delivery vector must be an XOR of donors of one
   entrance class. *Proved:* pivots ≤ |C| − rank = 263 − 86 = **177**, and rank-1 coordinate entrances lose nothing up to parity. *Exact maximum on the retimed R715 word: **112**, by a computer-assisted exhaustive search (independently re-audited), certified by
   `code/exact_pivots.py`* (rerun by `verify.py --light`, asserted equal to 112, about 10 s): the pivot problem is a min-sum-rank list partition (max pivots = |C| − min Σ_i rank of the class
   vectors; NP-hard in general, not a matroid union/intersection/parity problem), solved exactly here by splitting the delivery matroid into components (208 / 28 / 14 elements plus 13 coloops),
   exhaustive span-tuple DP on the small ones (16 and 9 pivots) and, on the 208, an exact block DP with a coupling-assignment lower bound and an exhaustive search (minimum sum-rank 121, so 87 pivots;
   120 shown infeasible): 87 + 16 + 9 = 112. The annealing plateau (14 of 16 restarts at 112, never 113) is therefore optimal. Priced by the model, a rank-1 pivot is worth ≈ +0.033% of c,
   so the pivot count on R715 is exhausted within this format (177 would have been ≈ +2.9%; it is not reachable; the donor choice among 112-pivot selections still moves c, README §3).
   *Scope:* the 177 and 586 are valid but loose scoped bounds; the 177 does not cover non-coordinate entrances. Upstream `kernel()` itself accepts any flat; there all 706 helpers qualify and the same argument
   gives only 706 − 120 = 586, in a format this package does not verify (it needs coordinate residual isometries). The exact 112 is a statement about the same coordinate, one-class-per-donor model;
   entrances at arbitrary root lines were only searched.
   *Follow-up:* the same exact method gives 101 pivots on the R687 read-then-climb word (100 after the parity rule); to be reported in a follow-up PR.
3. **The method:** `select_kernel.py` anneals the class assignment on the exact objective Σ rank (self-contained xorshift64*, reproducible from a seed),
   `kernel_from_selection.py` builds the word with #443's kernel unchanged. Pinned: `--seed 3 --iters 150000`.
4. Honest size: by kernel choice alone, without retiming or reordering, the first 112-pivot selection (c = 1.295564·10⁻³) landed, in κ, within 0.003% of #473 as first posted (1.293922·10⁻³);
   the shipped best-of-eight seed was 0.027% above that. #473 has since been updated (1.295630·10⁻³) and is 0.108% above this PR. This is selection tuning, not a ≥ 1% result.

**Verification** (`python -B research/e8-r715-kernel-cap/verify.py /abs/out [--light]`; CI workflow `e8-r715-kernel-cap`): LIGHT (about two minutes) checks integrity and
pins, recomputes the ceiling analysis from the pinned R715 word, **recomputes the exact pivot maximum and asserts 112**, checks the selection against #443's exact kernel conditions plus the F₂ response relation and the coordinate-flat condition,
rebuilds the kernel word (replay, interface) and the mixed word and compares them, checks the width rule, re-solves the hosting (CP-SAT) and prices it with the
exact engine, and runs the screen composition with #458's pinned endpoint. FULL adds the seeded search, #443's regressions, the relaxed all-column checker,
C++ cohort legality and formal columns at five and eleven stages, mixing mutants, Gram, eleven-stage template/audits, **hosting selection rediscovered with HiGHS and
required equal**, hosted audit, assembly, the pivot-count scan, #458's complex supplier from scratch, and the exact composition (two moment engines per side, six
bootstrap levels, all 47 strict outer inequalities, next-grid / zero-η / zero-β / unit-β rejection).

**Review points**
- The ceiling's proof (items 1–4 of README §2) is elementary. The new claim is the exact maximum 112: its certificate is the code in `code/exact_pivots.py` (component split, block DP,
  coupling lower bound, exhaustive search), rerun in LIGHT; please review that code and the min-sum-rank formulation of README §2 items 2–3 it relies on.
- The seed choice among equal pivot counts is an exact-priced selection (c between 1.295564 and 1.295911·10⁻³ across eight seeds).
- Inherited and unchanged: #450's Lemma M (bit target mixing, chained receivers), #458's paid adapters, the R715 hierarchy and its carrier bound (#463).
- The bit side is now 0.1% under #458's complex endpoint; further bit gains here are complex-capped.
Conditional like all parents; no unconditional theorem or Lean proof is claimed.

#440/#441), DaysSky (#442 idle-axis hosting), Dylan Crow (#370 word, producer, checkers), Srikrishnabalaji (#465), Dugongue (#471, #476, #478), jacklightChen and Zhihao Chen
(#386/#425), icekylinx (#433), higherbeing (#448), Jacob Sussman and all source-pinned authors. ## New: a shared-donor response kernel on the complex supplier

#433's split-centre complex word cancels each helper's dirt with frame-zero target additions (`compensation`, 12,760 rational adds), just as the bit word does with its D gates. The #417 kernel therefore carries over with rational coefficients:

- an entry is (e, p, d, λ) with **response(p) = λ·response(d)** exactly over ℚ, and e in the first frames of p and d;
- p starts at ⟨e⟩ and leaves the compensation;
- d += −λp at ⟨e⟩ before A, and d += λp at FULL after cleanup.

The word has exactly **56 proportional helper pairs**, and every pair shares an entrance vector. That gives 56 pivots, 56 donors and entrance rank 56, so 56 complex residuals shrink from width 9 to width 8. Width-8 residuals pack exactly into the rank-8k idle children, so the remainder children drop:
- complex profile `{1:174864, 2:78848, 3:8680, 4:19712, 5:38120, 7:2944, 8:8000, 30:8, 64:2160}`;
- deficit 3264, all 49,280 occurrences still hosted, no banks.

body:
Conditional **κ = 1330733966732373/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.330733966732373·10⁻³**, bit-bound, **+5.13 % over #447** (1.265848755025709·10⁻³, complex-bound), +7.53 % over #442 and +17.44 % over #434. Neither local word changes: complex #433 (R = 560, m = 73), bit #434 (R = 747, m = 64). The idle windows are #442's.

## Change

In #442's idle-axis hosting a whole helper residual sits inside the pending coordinates of one data family. Bit residuals have width 8 − e (637 of width 8, 104 of width 7, 6 of width 4) and complex residuals width 9, while the idle children have ranks 7/14/28/42 (bit) and 8/16/32/48 (complex). A rank-7 child cannot hold a width-8 residual, a rank-14 child holds one and wastes six coordinates, and so on: 6,944 of the 45,360 pending bit coordinates per replica and 5,760 of 51,840 complex ones stay idle and are paid as remainder children.

A child acts on every copy (side, port) of its pair, and all copies share the child's window. This package lets a residual lie across the pending sets of **two copies of the same idle child**. With P = P₁ + P₂ the identity D_{P₁}·D_{P₂} = D_P (the parents' D_{P'}·D_{P−P'} = D_P) writes the dirty invocation's factor on the residual as a product of a factor on each family; each is moved to the child exactly as in #442 §2, since the window is a property of the pair; and each child's remainder is exact by #442's fact (b). Every child's capacity, copies × rank, is then a multiple of the residual width, so the remainders almost vanish. A residual never spans two children or two pairs. The route is still an elementary coordinate permutation of the address space; the finite invoice charges one further route factor per helper selector.

The selection is an integer programme over counts n(child, stage, width) on the concatenated tape of each child's copies (maximise Σ ln(m/r) × hosted coordinates, subject to availability and, on the bit side, exact width-64 tiling of the leftover). `SELECTION.json` freezes it; `--discover` recomputes it with scipy.

## Result

| supplier | #442 saving | this saving | live stock | hosted residuals (split) | max child |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bit, m = 64, R = 747 | 1.239085·10⁻³ | **1.332507·10⁻³** | 9,457 → 8,592 | 46,160 of 53,784 (12,496) | 24 |
| complex, m = 73, R = 560 | 1.267453·10⁻³ | **1.437532·10⁻³** | 8,400 → 7,680 | 40,320 of 40,320 (13,720) | 48 |

Both rank deficits stay 2496. The bit max child 24 is one partial copy of a rank-28 child; the complex max child 48 is the 133 copies per replica of the rank-48 final children that the complex supply cannot fill (5,040 residuals against 5,760 width-9 slots per replica). Since #447 is complex-bound at 1.267453·10⁻³, the complex component here should also lift #445/#447's eleven-stage bit words; that composition is not claimed.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/cross-copy-hosting/verify.py /absolute/new/output` (Python 3.11+, standard library only; the output directory must not exist). It

1. runs #434's complete verifier from scratch;
2. regenerates both hosted templates from #434's fresh outputs and the frozen selection;
3. runs an independent audit that shares no code with the generators: windows re-derived from each schedule; for every replica and invocation exactly one owner record per helper; every hosted residual has one or two pieces on copies of the child it names, widths summing to the residual width, inside the pending set, pairwise disjoint per (child, copy), inside the window and off the active pair; exact remainder children and bank tilings; profile, live stock and deficit 2496 recomputed; twelve mutation controls rejected (including a split across two children and a split whose widths do not sum to the residual width);
4. prices both suppliers with the two inherited rational moment engines and fresh finite invoices (prefix 226 bits charged 256, two-level coefficient 488 bits charged 512, row coefficient 18,355 < 20,161; complex row coefficient 15,443);
5. runs #434's strict outer assembly: six bootstrap levels and all 47 inequalities, with the next grid point and the zero-η, zero-β and unit-β controls rejected.

Local transcript: `PASS_FULL_CROSS_COPY_HOSTING_COMPOSITION` on macOS (Apple silicon), Python 3.14.3, 5 min 48 s including the full #434 replay; every value equals `EXPECTED.json` and both template hashes match. CI is not claimed before it runs.

## Scope

This is a written finite extension of #442's hosting interface: a helper residual's physical slot may lie in two data families of one idle child. That is the principal new review point; [PROOF.md](research/cross-copy-hosting/PROOF.md) gives the argument from the parents' two facts. #442's own extension (helper residuals on data streams during idle windows) and all inherited interfaces remain assumptions: the all-size compiler, correlated dirty-bank and compressed-window interfaces, restored work, tape/common grid, precision and analytic transfer. The global operator identity is argued and checked combinatorially, not replayed numerically on the address spaces. No Lean proof and no unconditional integer-multiplication theorem is claimed.

The cross-copy selection, generators, audit, assembly and proof note were prepared by higherbeing with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance.

### Construction and attribution

**icekylinx, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**, supplies the split-centre Hamming construction, reversible source-centre bit construction, integration and checks in [PR433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/433), pinned at `6d9244518175caf9e0089f92486959bc2c317273`. **Zhihao Chen, with OpenAI Codex assistance**, supplies PR425's mutable-basis Hamming/common-frame interface and PR386's compressed bit geometry, owner template and accounting. **ai-nanachi, with OpenAI Codex assistance**, supplies the unchanged PR426 R767 word used before the source-centre replacements. The original carried geometry receipt is retained as provenance and is not labeled a fresh regeneration. The defining decoder satisfies the required integer construction and parity projection; the unsigned XOR word is not presented as an integer-identity certificate. The signed correction needs **8537 weighted additions, including 245 even coefficients**, or **8978 signed unit additions** versus **8292 parity units**. The Gaussian block proof rounds to the p-grid and then asserts an error bound that can be smaller than any possible grid error. For the exact scalar value h/2, with P=p+12 and unit chirp factors, the asserted bound is h/8, whereas every p-grid value is at distance at least h/2.

Label that bound as the internal, pre-extraction enclosure and account separately for the <sqrt(2)h complex component-truncation error. Retain the fine dyadic block value until the S' normalization or E subtraction is complete. Exact rational normalization followed by fine-grid truncation preserves the existing <3h forward and <5h correction-map budgets, under the other estimates used in the source proof. The stated output allowances and asymptotic cost are unchanged.

The rounding defect and counterexample were identified by GPT-6 Pro. Codex independently confirmed the exact arithmetic and propagated the correction through these two calculations. Existing eumemic/icekylinx and Harvey–van der Hoeven attribution is retained. This is an AI-generated and AI-reviewed correction, with no human or formal verification claimed. It does not supply a new multiplication exponent or verify the inherited analytic/source hypotheses.

The correction is conditional on the parameter bounds already used in the chirp calculations, including theta<=1/4 and sigma<2. The referenced no-sort lemma header is broader; this patch does not resolve that inherited domain mismatch or certify the containing lemma at its full printed scope.

Validation: the independent exact counterexample already passed the pinned local runner. The added small standard-library checker verifies the scalar witness and rational endpoint budgets. Exact replay, patch-application, and immutable source receipts accompany the review packet.

## Change and mathematical scope

[PR288 §1.4(d)](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/288) already reports the restricted sign-gauge obstruction for the Braverman–He PG(2,9) instance. This contribution supplies an explicit four-constraint witness, three inspectable five-edge paths and a separate exact verifier. Two session signs are forced to be both equal and opposite. **No new multiplication bound, κ, exponent or practical speedup is claimed.**

The model has fixed additive 5×5 rational vertex matrices, rank-at-most-one physical edge differences and independently signed session targets equal to one common invertible matrix. The result does not cover nonadditive or varying frames, unrelated Levi targets, higher-rank edges or larger dimensions. The matrix-to-sign implication is an ordinary written proof, not a Lean proof, independent human peer review or verification of the full multiplication theorem. Unprovided SAT/MITM/Gröbner searches are outside this contribution.

The standalone package contains the normalized instance, certificate, proof, independent checker, deterministic producer and 24 corruption/positive-control tests. Its checker imports neither the producer nor upstream checker. A new Make target and split CI job check the package; existing algorithms and witnesses are unchanged. Scope: ten research files, five Makefile lines and nineteen workflow lines.

Sources are pinned to upstream main `12a4934d15006e8c10f9b2264f13f8f341be802b` and PR288's head `475a088b5862f75f0b10596cfd6842d19531a5ec` in eumemic/integer-mult-bounds. Inputs remained unchanged and mathematical certificates were byte-identical. This preserves the host result; it is not a new result of this sign-cycle contribution.

Baseline stopped in `scripts/complex_network.py`; candidate stopped in `scripts/paired_network.py`, both within `verify-certificates`. Later groups are not cleared. The gen4 successes above refer to the completed embedded runs.

Historical `SOURCE.json` expects Makefile SHA-256 `768131bd4ce18433f6abccdc9812a38c92e11220e3a1019c6d95334b42f529d1`; pristine baseline is `cd0fb59dc078d1fdf54a163ea13bb3660d03c8fe69c1a7f99fc8e5f476a3d5c2`, candidate is `bfe01daff2349b7260d6580ee2b1ce149fddf98ac1a59aca5bbca102299f0958`.

## Original pinned PR302 contribution

## Summary

Add a standalone verifier and construction note for 70 shared-donor rank-one kernel pivots, composed with pinned [PR300](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/300) and the 12-helper co-retiming from [PR301](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/301). - Exact conditional kappa: `749940157923873/10^18 = 0.000749940157923873`.

Comparisons here use the pinned older heads; newer upstream revisions exist, and this PR does not claim the best current bound.

## What is new

Pivots may share donors on the same rank-one entrance line. Pivot and donor sets remain disjoint, so the shear incidence matrix squares to zero and the setup/restore factors commute. Exact response relations, a reproduced common read cut and complete local frame paths certify the changed bit construction compositionally under the inherited decoder.

The packet includes independent role-to-bank allocation, not just inventory arithmetic: all 15,427 helper roles and all 60 replicas are assigned, totaling 925,620 assignments per stage and 4,628,100 across five disjoint stage namespaces. All 440 restoration and seven sink entries match PR299 semantically. Exact determinants additionally verify 65 distinct selected PR300 bases. The finite bill includes all 1,202 new scalar additions per stage and the actual sink redirects/mixed target paths.

## Immutable dependencies and diff scope

Fixed backoffs and a fixed bootstrap depth leave a gap below the retained balanced assembly's supplied-cap ceiling. This PR adds a constructive finite-parameter theorem, an exact verifier, and source-bound applications to PR433 and PR799. The source-basis, contract-checking and E8 contributions below remain included.

### Review coverage (2026-10-13)

The [published upstream review](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/50d768818f579d4e165b4c257c6ee25bca300802/docs/research/community-reconciliation-next100-review.md) and [review comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/275#issuecomment-6158132521) record that **the two primary finite-assembly packages passed**, including the pinned PR799 application, at this exact head. PR275 remains open with partial coverage: the other research/tooling packages require individual review and execution. Inherited generic CI does not cover the whole expanded submission.

Additional contributor-side validation at this unchanged head:

- `research/e8-exact-bank-optimizer`: all four existing tests passed, including the independent 16,875-inventory oracle, pinned witness cases, large compressed counts, architecture constraints and rejection controls. The proof and implementation were reviewed; all three public pattern fixtures matched their source commits. This establishes the stated finite bank result under its fixed-inventory premises.
- `research/e8-dirty-chart-audit`: all six existing tests passed. The PR416 control preserves its normalized dirty inputs; the original and changed PR419 fixtures produce the expected endpoint counterexamples in both orientations. Tests also cover a witness first appearing after address zero and exact operator cancellations. The two vendored implementations matched their immutable public sources, and all four fixtures matched their retained source bytes. This validates the diagnostic, without admitting PR419 or excluding a different coupled-bank construction.
- `research/e8-hosted-bit-contract`: all four existing tests and the exact two-line in-memory audit integration passed on the authentic pinned PR442 bit fixture. The guard accepts the intact schedule and rejects the deliberate terminal-exchange and bridge-coefficient regressions, which the original audit accepts with unchanged profiles. The verifier checked retained reconstruction receipts; the seven reconstruction stages were not rerun. The five public source/notice/license/receipt files matched their immutable revision. This strengthens verification and does not claim that the actual PR442 construction is invalid.

- `research/e8-emitter-digest-cache`: the unchanged offline verifier passed all 2,742,552 record-byte comparisons across 144 calls, matching complete digests, event counts and paid instruction profiles, plus both focused encoding/cache-lifetime tests. The proof and source-extracted loop were reviewed against the immutable PR447 emitter. Original source, license, notice and manifest matched their public revision.
- `research/e8-scalar-address-cache`: the unchanged offline verifier passed two complete 9,417-column, eleven-stage scalar replays, 648,692 operand comparisons, all 24 bridge omission controls per fixture and both focused address-boundary/cache-lifetime tests. Exact patch scope and composition with the digest cache passed. Both packages use the retained completed PR438/PR442 workloads; no benchmark or complete supplier stage was rerun. Their documented speedups remain historical microbenchmark measurements, not new end-to-end claims.

- `research/e8-bit-basis-order`: the unchanged offline audit and all three existing postprocessor tests passed. It checks all 998 PR433 and 987 PR438 literal source/target/helper columns in both orientations, equal copied forms, inverse/dirty-compensator rejection, and exact prefix/finite-coefficient arithmetic. The coefficient sizes reproduce 223→192 and 226→193 bits; the two-level sizes reproduce 483→420 and 488→423 bits, with all 32 extra local additions charged in each case. Tests cover input preservation, idempotence, six unsafe interfaces and CLI overwrite refusal. Four public source files matched their immutable revisions. The five/nine supplier-stage and complex-component receipts are retained evidence, not fresh supplier or phase replays; the PR438 baseline coefficient is reconstructed algebraically. Caps and κ are unchanged.

These were bounded CPython 3.14.8 runs. Submitted package bytes and manifests are unchanged. The bank and dirty-chart verifiers used a disclosed startup shim that adds `-E -S` to their single unittest child; the hosted-bit and both cache verifiers ran unchanged under `-E -S -B` with in-process tests. The basis default audit and its three tests ran under `-E -S -B`, with those startup flags also added to the two exact postprocessor CLI calls, including the expected overwrite refusal. The coordinating Codex session separately reviewed source and rehashed runtime/input pins and execution receipts. This is AI-assisted contributor validation. Upstream acceptance of these additional packages remains pending; no new supplier, native-cost or κ improvement follows.

### Finite assembly theorem

For admitted rational bit and complex caps `c,b`, put `a0 = 384599/10^10` and `u = min(b,c)`. Under `a0 < u`, `b < 1/32`, an admitted finite coefficient charge, and the inherited weighted-bootstrap and bridge premises, every rational

```text
0 < kappa < u/(1+u)
```

has a finite constructible witness. The constructor selects positive backoffs, finitely many bootstrap levels and explicit integer cutoffs, then checks all 47 retained strict inequalities. The proof establishes termination and the greatest admissible point on any supplied rational grid. This ceiling is relative to the supplied caps and this assembly family; the endpoint is never attained.

Start with the [proof](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c/research/finite-assembly-frontier/PROOF.md), [constructor](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c/research/finite-assembly-frontier/assembly.py) and [historical package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c/research/finite-assembly-frontier). The complete 51-file historical package is retained unchanged from `e819106`, including its PR433 fixture, five behavioral tests, source notices and receipts. It remains self-contained for default offline verification.

### Source-bound PR799 application

The [PR799 adapter](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c/research/finite-assembly-pr799) applies that same theorem to the maintainer-admitted native-complex PR799 and unchanged PR589 bit supplier at upstream `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`.

| Conditional value | Kappa |
| --- | --- |
| Pinned PR799 baseline | `0.001661634653669567` |
| Finite witness on the `10^-27` grid | `0.001661634653669567075843432` |

The difference is only `7.5843432e-20`. The contribution is a reusable theorem and reproducible admission interface. This parameter improvement is not a substantive frontier advance, new supplier construction or practical speedup. The [upstream reconciliation at `50d7688`](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/50d768818f579d4e165b4c257c6ee25bca300802/docs/research/community-reconciliation-next100-review.md) retains the selected conditional frontier `0.001672660197076918`, above this historical PR799 application. No current numerical lead is claimed here.

The adapter verifies 144 immutable upstream file bindings and the unchanged core package. It uses the original PR741/PR799 receipt checkers and admission code, binds the exact integrated replay's owner and invoice, reproduces the complete published assembly, and then constructs the new witness with nine finite levels. Both rational engines check the selected seed; all finite cutoffs and 47 strict inequalities pass. The next grid point and ceiling endpoint are rejected, as are zero eta, zero beta and unit beta.

Recurrence policy is explicit: native complex omits the bad-residue surcharge; bit retains it. Conservative admission runs first. The complex finite invoice is recomputed. The unchanged bit coefficient bound `393 < 512` and row bound `18355` are reused through the authenticated PR589 records; the underlying bit coefficient integer and physical suppliers are not rebuilt.

### Reproduction and validation

Historical example:

```sh
python3 -B research/finite-assembly-frontier/verify.py
```

Pinned PR799 application, after obtaining the pinned upstream snapshot using the [README commands](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c/research/finite-assembly-pr799/README.md):

```sh
python3 -E -S -B research/finite-assembly-pr799/verify.py \
  --upstream ../integer-mult-pr799-upstream \
  --output ../integer-mult-pr799-result
```

The verifier runs offline with Python 3.11+ and the standard library. It records exact parameters, cutoffs, moment intervals, constraints and completion hashes. A local bounded validation reproduced the complete portable result and rejected three isolated source mutations before scientific imports: sibling README, upstream input and core input. Original inputs remained unchanged. Root independently checked the source bindings, execution receipts and exact rational result; Ody performed the bounded runs and independent workflow review.

Current head: [`524375c`](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/commit/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c). All 60 jobs passed across the five existing fork push workflows on this exact commit: [research/formal verification](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38392189883), [graded box convolution](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38392190153), [terminal elimination](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38392190102), [recycled bit registers](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38392189936) and [early reset/kernel composition](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38392189908). These existing workflows do not include a dedicated PR799 adapter job; the new adapter is covered by the bounded local validation described above. Upstream pull-request workflows separately report `action_required` without running jobs. Fork CI does not establish upstream approval.

### Other contributions retained

These packages retain their source bindings, proofs, validation receipts and attribution. Recorded performance figures refer to the original scoped benchmarks.

**Research closeout — Draft retained; no current-record claim.** This is an exact fixed-prime arithmetic refinement of [PR #259](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/259). It inherits #259's finite physical construction and changes the conditional bit-supplier calculation only.

## Result and contribution boundary

```text
PR #259: 142205877210807 / 200000000000000000
PR #261: 711029389987426878345881 / 10^27
Exact gain: 3933391878345881 / 10^27
```

At `m = 120`, the certificate fixes `q = 2^127 - 1`, uses rare-class density `rho = 3456000/q < 10^-16`, and charges the complete `32m^2` rare-child fallback. It retains #259's 518 pivot entrances, four cuts, physical frames, routes, roles, replicas and lifetimes unchanged. It makes no new physical-DAG saving.

The finite arithmetic replay regenerates the cohort profile and invoice, uses two rational interval engines for the coarse endpoint, checks eight finite levels, 47 strict outer constraints and seven margins, and rejects the adjacent `10^-27` grid point. The fresh finite coefficient is `62639910650427201 < 2^80 < q`; selector, chart, normalizer, signed-prefix and inherited physical costs remain charged.

**Attribution:** Dugongue's #259 provides the inherited multi-cut physical witness and invoice; its pinned source lineage comes from #249. The fixed-prime approach credits Nespoli #235 and Arun #252, with #255/#258 refinements acknowledged in the certificate history. The exact recomputation, certificate, documentation and workflow integration in this PR were prepared by sennemmi with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Upstream authorship, source notices and license files are retained; the added package carries its stated Apache-2.0 license.

## Incremental review path

The full PR comparison against `main` is large because it carries the upstream research lineage: GitHub reports 422 changed files and 1,707,820 additions. Removing inherited source or receipts would weaken provenance or replayability, so this closeout keeps them intact. The independently reviewable increment is exactly one commit over #259 SHA `a53ec0ca4d59634f16630dd16adf035c9f12595c` at head `d2c63486d895860a65f25b80a51f4b2ec4f3c6ef`: [compare #259 to #261](https://github.com/sennemmi/integer-mult-bounds/compare/a53ec0ca4d59634f16630dd16adf035c9f12595c...d2c63486d895860a65f25b80a51f4b2ec4f3c6ef). That increment has 14 files:

1. `README.md`, `PROOF.md` — statement, arithmetic mechanism and limits.
2. `fixed_prime_math.py`, `expected.json` — exact recomputation and pinned result.
3. `verify.py`, `SOURCE.json`, `MANIFEST.json` — source pins, integrity checks and replay.
4. `Prime.lean`, `lakefile.toml`, `lean-toolchain` — kernel-checked prime/density facts only.
5. `LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md`, `requirements.txt` — provenance, license and dependencies.
6. `.github/workflows/multicut-fixed-prime.yml` — replay and Lean job.

## Reproduction and verification

## Change

A second exact frame retiming of #251's regauged source527 ADD word. Twenty-five internal `forward_gate` ADD frames (25 of 786,623 gates) are reassigned by local descent on the concave paid-rank objective Σ r·ln(120/r), using only frames already present on the operands' chains. The local paid histogram changes by {2: −2, 4: +24, 5: −48, 6: +25, 11: −1, 13: +2, 17: −1}: one local recursive call per helper invocation disappears at unchanged rank mass 433,953. The literal construction keeps 24 replicas, stock 521,425 and deficit 105,600 with 11,792,160 paid calls (was 11,792,280); the per-replica bank call count is 491,340 (was 491,345). Banks, charts, entrances, prime witnesses, the scalar word and every endpoint are unchanged.

Why this is the whole retiming budget: for the window (prev, cur, next) of a register the objective is concave in dim(cur), so each gate is optimal at either the minimal frame (join of the operands' previous frames and their source spans) or the maximal frame (meet of the next frames). On #251's word 99.7 % of gates have those two coincide with the current frame; the fully eager (greatest-fixpoint) assignment is worse (Σ r·ln(120/r) = 1.1817 × 10⁶ vs 1.1374 × 10⁶), and block moves (raising or lowering whole runs between ascents) are blocked by partner chains or source spans. ## Idea

#207 showed that PR200's operation frames are not optimal for the paid moment, and admitted 302 frame changes. This PR pushes the same lever much further.

- **Chain model.** Every physical chain of PR200's word is modeled exactly: splices, root frames and the full endpoint. Each operation frame is shared by its two chains. A frame is feasible when it:
  - contains the value span;
  - is G-nondegenerate;
  - is nested between its neighbours on both chains.

  Each chain costs Σ t·ln(72/t) over its rank increments.
- **Cascading moves.**
  - Raise a frame to a later neighbour (up to four slots ahead) or to the global feasible maximum, joining forward to repair nesting.
  - Lower it to an earlier neighbour or the global minimum, meeting backward.
  - Root frames, gauge frames, start frames and alias endpoints stay fixed.
  - Greedy plus short annealing reaches an optimum where single-op moves stall.
  - Result: 6,191 frames change, and internal chain cost falls 0.135%.
- **Admission.** Only frames change, and PR200's own modules re-check:
  - value spans, nondegeneracy, all chain nestings and the 1,760 alias containments;

## Change and mathematical scope

A new finite-network construction, the **zeta family**, on the Boolean lattice. Inputs are all nonzero, non-full bitmasks of `[h]`; the DAG is the **fast Yates zeta transform**; the side root for target `t` is `Z_{full^t}` = the sum of every input submasked into `complement(t)`, i.e. bit-disjoint from `t`. The in-tree side-root orthogonality contract (value span inside the orthogonal complement of the targets' addresses) holds **by construction**. No center roots, so `ell = 0` and the in-tree identity gives `deficit = 2v`. The binding quantity is the role density `R/v`.
